def search(self, evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> None:
    """Run the search of one experiment.

    The default runs the step interface: ``start``, then the step loop shown in the
    [module docs][SRToolkit.approaches.approach]. Approaches without the step interface
    override it, keeping the search state in local variables (see the lifecycle in the module
    docs). Score expressions with ``evaluate_expr``; the framework collects the results.
    ``evaluate_expr`` returns the expression's
    [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult], with its error, fitted ``parameters``
    and ``status``.

    Search while ``evaluator.should_stop`` is ``False``; it turns ``True`` when the success
    threshold or the budget is reached, a callback stops the run, or the run is interrupted
    (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM). To end the search early (e.g. the search space is exhausted), call
    [evaluator.stop][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.stop] with a reason, so
    the results explain why; returning without it is recorded as ``"returned"``.

    The symbol library is available in ``evaluator.symbol_library``. ``evaluator.describe()``
    gives the task as text (e.g. for an LLM prompt) and ``evaluator.background_knowledge`` as
    objects. Do not read ``evaluator.ground_truth``: it is the answer. Report expressions
    discarded without evaluation as skips (see [Skips][SRToolkit.approaches.approach]).

    Args:
        evaluator: Evaluator used to score expressions. All results are
            stored inside this object.
        seed: Optional random seed for reproducible expression generation.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If the approach implements neither ``search`` nor ``ask``, or
            implements ``ask`` without ``start``.
    """
    if not self.supports_steps:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"[{type(self).__name__}] implements neither search() nor the step interface (start/ask/tell)."
        )
    self._step_loop(evaluator, self.start(evaluator, seed))

Run the approach on evaluator: continue from its snapshot, or search anew.

If evaluator.resumed_from holds a Snapshot, the search state is restored with load_search_state, then the global random states, and the step loop continues; neither start nor search is called, and errors of load_search_state propagate. Otherwise it calls search. If the search returns while evaluation goes on, run stops it with the reason "returned", so the checkpoint records the run as finished. evaluate_approach and ExperimentJob.run call it.

def run(self, evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> None:
    """Run the approach on ``evaluator``: continue from its snapshot, or search anew.

    If ``evaluator.resumed_from`` holds a
    [Snapshot][SRToolkit.evaluation.model_store.Snapshot], the search state is restored with
    [load_search_state][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.load_search_state], then
    the global random states, and the step loop continues; neither ``start`` nor ``search`` is
    called, and errors of ``load_search_state`` propagate. Otherwise it calls [search][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.search]. If the
    search returns while evaluation goes on, ``run`` stops it with the reason ``"returned"``,
    so the checkpoint records the run as finished.
    [evaluate_approach][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.evaluate_approach] and
    [ExperimentJob.run][SRToolkit.experiments.ExperimentJob.run] call it.

    Args:
        evaluator: The evaluator, new or resumed.
        seed: The seed passed to ``search`` for a new run; ignored when continuing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the evaluator holds a snapshot but the approach lacks the step
            interface.
    """
    snapshot = evaluator.resumed_from
    if snapshot is None:
        self.search(evaluator, seed)
    else:
        if not self.supports_steps:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[{type(self).__name__}] cannot continue from a snapshot: it lacks the step interface "
                "(start/ask/tell)."
            )
        state = self.load_search_state(snapshot.state)
        _restore_rngs(snapshot.rngs)
        self._step_loop(evaluator, state)
    if not evaluator.should_stop:
        evaluator.stop("returned")

def start(self, evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> Any:

    the first ``ask`` does that. Do not change the approach object: everything the run changes

def ask(self, evaluator: Evaluator, state: Any) -> "list[Candidate | list[str] | Expression | None]":
    """Propose the next expressions to evaluate (step interface).

    The first call after ``start`` creates them from scratch (e.g. a random population); later
    calls build on what ``tell`` stored in ``state``. It may change ``state`` (e.g. remember
    what it proposed) but not the approach object, and may use the unbilled ``get_model``,
    ``stored_tokens`` and ``check_constraints`` of ``evaluator``, but not ``evaluate_expr``.
    An empty list ends the search, as if ``search`` had returned; to record why, call
    ``evaluator.stop(reason)`` first. To discard an
    expression without evaluating it, propose it with a ``skip`` reason (see
    [Skips][SRToolkit.approaches.approach]).

    Args:
        evaluator: The evaluator of the run.
        state: The search state from ``start`` or ``load_search_state``, the same object for
            the whole session, as earlier ``ask`` and ``tell`` calls left it.

    Returns:
        The expressions, in the order they are to be evaluated: token lists or
        [Expression][SRToolkit.utils.expression.Expression]s (with specs), or
        [Candidate][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Candidate]s to mark a skip. If the approach
        also passes an expression to ``get_model``, ``stored_tokens`` or
        ``check_constraints``, pass the same ``Expression`` object here, so it is parsed once.
        ``None`` marks a proposal that is not an expression (e.g. a latent vector that does not

Serialise the search state for a snapshot (step interface).

Called between steps when a snapshot is due, when the loop ends, and, with a checkpoint, once before the first step of every session (new or resumed) with the result discarded, so a state that cannot be saved fails before any budget is spent. The state must include the approach's own random generators and anything the search fine-tunes (e.g. model weights). The global random states (Python, NumPy, PyTorch) are saved by the framework; what adaptation set up lives in the approach object and is restored before load_search_state.

def dump_search_state(self, state: Any) -> bytes:
    """Serialise the search state for a snapshot (step interface).

    Called between steps when a snapshot is due, when the loop ends, and, with a checkpoint,
    once before the first step of every session (new or resumed) with the result discarded, so a state that cannot be saved fails
    before any budget is spent. It must not change ``state``: the run continues with it. The
    default pickles it and raises whatever ``pickle`` raises if the state does not pickle;
    override it then, or to leave out what ``load_search_state`` can rebuild. The state must
    include the approach's own random generators and anything the search fine-tunes (e.g.
    model weights). The global random states (Python, NumPy, PyTorch) are saved by the
    framework; what adaptation set up lives in the approach object and is restored before
    ``load_search_state``.

    Args:
        state: The search state.

    Returns:
        The serialised state.
    """
    return pickle.dumps(state)

@classmethod
def from_config_dict(cls, config: dict) -> "Approach":
    """Reconstruct an approach from a config dict that includes an ``approach_class`` path.

    This is the self-dispatching counterpart to
    [from_config][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.from_config]: it binds the
    config to any installed ``.srtk`` bundle, resolves the concrete approach class named
    by ``approach_class``, and delegates to that class's
    [from_config][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.from_config]. Mirrors
    [Dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.from_dict], which
    resolves its own class the same way.

    Args:
        config: A serialised approach config containing an ``approach_class`` key, as
            produced by
            [ApproachConfig.to_dict][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.ApproachConfig.to_dict].

    Returns:
        A new instance of the concrete approach class.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``approach_class`` cannot be imported (e.g. its ``.srtk`` bundle
            is not installed, or the config has no ``_bundle`` key and was never bound).
        TypeError: If ``approach_class`` is not an Approach subclass.
    """
    config = _auto_bind(config)
    target_cls = _import_class(config["approach_class"], "approach", Approach)
    return target_cls.from_config(config)

Serialisable base configuration for SR approaches.

Subclass this dataclass to define approach-specific hyperparameters that can be saved and restored via to_dict and from_dict. Fields must hold values that can be saved (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, numpy arrays, …; see serialization).

>>> d = cfg.to_dict()

def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any:
    """Import ``EDHiE`` and ``EDHiEConfig`` on first access (PEP 562).

    Returns:
        The requested class, or a placeholder that raises ``ImportError`` on instantiation if
        PyTorch or pymoo is not installed.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If ``name`` is not a lazily imported attribute of this package.
    """
    if name not in _LAZY_EDHIE:
        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    try:
        module = _importlib.import_module(".EDHiE", __name__)
        values = {attr: getattr(module, attr) for attr in _LAZY_EDHIE}
    except ImportError as error:
        values = _missing_dependency_stubs(error)
    globals().update(values)
    return values[name]

def __init__(
    self,
    latent_size: int = 32,
    num_expressions: int = 20000,
    max_expression_length: int = 30,
    only_unique_expressions: bool = True,
    epochs: int = 20,
    batch_size: int = 32,
    max_beta: float = 0.035,
    population_size: int = 40,
    weights_path: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
    max_training_skips: int = 10000,
    skip_evaluated: bool = True,
    skip_rejected: bool = True,
    training_seed: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    r"""EDHiE: equation discovery with hierarchical variational autoencoders by Mežnar et al.

    [adapt][SRToolkit.approaches.EDHiE.EDHiE.adapt] trains a hierarchical VAE (HVAE) on random
    expressions for the task; the search runs a genetic algorithm in its latent space. In the
    [step interface][SRToolkit.approaches.approach], one step is one generation and is never
    empty, so the search runs until the evaluator stops it.

    A stopped run resumes only with the same HVAE, bit for bit: load it from a file
    (``weights_path`` or a saved adapted state), or train it again with the same
    ``training_seed`` on the same device and PyTorch version. Other settings are not checked.

    Args:
        latent_size: Dimension of the HVAE latent space.
        num_expressions: Number of training expressions.
        max_expression_length: Longest training expression, in tokens.
        only_unique_expressions: Train on distinct expressions while the grammar yields new ones
            (see [training_expressions][SRToolkit.approaches.EDHiE.EDHiE.training_expressions]).
            ``False`` keeps repeats, so likely expressions weigh more.
        epochs: Number of HVAE training epochs.
        batch_size: HVAE training batch size.
        max_beta: Largest KL weight of the annealing schedule (regularisation strength).
        population_size: GA population size. A resumed run keeps the snapshot's.
        weights_path: File written by [save_adapted_state][SRToolkit.approaches.EDHiE.EDHiE.save_adapted_state];
            the HVAE is loaded from it here and used for every task.
        verbose: Print the training loss and reconstructions while training (the search prints nothing).
        max_training_skips: Limit for sampling the training expressions (see
            ``training_expressions``). It does not limit the search; the setting
            ``evaluator.max_consecutive_skips`` does.
        skip_evaluated: Skip expressions evaluated before (see [ask][SRToolkit.approaches.EDHiE.EDHiE.ask]).
            ``False`` evaluates them again, as cache hits that use the budget.
        skip_rejected: Skip expressions that break a required constraint. ``False`` evaluates
            them, so they use the budget and appear in the results as ``"rejected"``.
        training_seed: Seed for ``adapt``, or ``None`` for unseeded.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``max_training_skips`` is below 1.

    Examples:
        >>> model = EDHiE(latent_size=24, num_expressions=100, epochs=1, verbose=False)
        >>> model.name
        'EDHiE'

    References:
        [Mežnar et al. (2023)][cite-edhie]
    """
    super().__init__(
        EDHiEConfig(
            latent_size=latent_size,
            num_expressions=num_expressions,
            max_expression_length=max_expression_length,
            only_unique_expressions=only_unique_expressions,
            epochs=epochs,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            max_beta=max_beta,
            population_size=population_size,
            weights_path=weights_path,
            verbose=verbose,
            max_training_skips=max_training_skips,
            skip_evaluated=skip_evaluated,
            skip_rejected=skip_rejected,
            training_seed=training_seed,
        )
    )
    if max_training_skips < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"[EDHiE] max_training_skips must be at least 1, got {max_training_skips}.")
    check_dependencies(["pytorch", "pymoo"])
    self.latent_size = latent_size
    self.num_expressions = num_expressions
    self.max_expression_length = max_expression_length
    self.only_unique_expressions = only_unique_expressions
    self.epochs = epochs
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.max_beta = max_beta
    self.population_size = population_size
    self.verbose = verbose
    self.max_training_skips = max_training_skips
    self.skip_evaluated = skip_evaluated
    self.skip_rejected = skip_rejected
    self.training_seed = training_seed

    self.model: HVAE | None = None
    self._pretrained = weights_path is not None
    if weights_path is not None:
        self.load_adapted_state(weights_path)

def adapt(
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    background_knowledge: "BackgroundKnowledge",
    required_constraints: Sequence[ExpressionConstraint],
) -> None:
    """Train a new HVAE on the task's training expressions, replacing any earlier one.

    The expressions come from [training_expressions][SRToolkit.approaches.EDHiE.EDHiE.training_expressions].
    With ``training_seed`` set, sampling and training are reproducible and the global random
    states are restored afterwards.

    Args:
        X: Not used.
        background_knowledge: Supplies the training expressions.
        required_constraints: Every training expression passes them.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no valid training expressions can be sampled.
    """
    # Seed this training only: the global states are restored afterwards, so later unseeded
    # searches stay random.
    states = None
    if self.training_seed is not None:
        states = (random.getstate(), np.random.get_state(), torch.get_rng_state())
        random.seed(self.training_seed)
        np.random.seed(self.training_seed)
        torch.manual_seed(self.training_seed)
    try:
        symbol_library = background_knowledge.symbol_library
        expressions = self.training_expressions(background_knowledge, required_constraints)
        expr_trees: list[Node | None] = [tokens_to_tree(expr, symbol_library) for expr in expressions]
        self.model = HVAE(len(symbol_library), self.latent_size, symbol_library)
        train_hvae(
            self.model,
            TreeDataset(expr_trees),
            symbol_library,
            epochs=self.epochs,
            batch_size=self.batch_size,
            max_beta=self.max_beta,
            verbose=self.verbose,
        )
    finally:
        if states is not None:
            random.setstate(states[0])
            np.random.set_state(states[1])
            torch.set_rng_state(states[2])

def training_expressions(
    self,
    background_knowledge: "BackgroundKnowledge",
    required_constraints: Sequence[ExpressionConstraint],
) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Sample the expressions the HVAE is trained on.

    Samples from [sampling_grammar][SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge.BackgroundKnowledge.sampling_grammar]
    and keeps those of at most ``max_expression_length`` tokens that pass the pre-checks of
    ``required_constraints``. With
    ``only_unique_expressions``, they are distinct until ``max_training_skips`` valid samples in a
    row are repeats; then repeats fill the rest, with a warning.

    Args:
        background_knowledge: Supplies the grammar.
        required_constraints: Set-up constraints every expression must pass.

    Returns:
        ``num_expressions`` token lists.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``max_training_skips`` samples in a row break a required constraint.
    """
    grammar = background_knowledge.sampling_grammar()
    symbol_library = background_knowledge.symbol_library
    constant = str(symbol_library.constant_symbol)

    expressions: list[list[str]] = []
    seen = set()
    allow_repeats = not self.only_unique_expressions
    rejected = repeats = 0  # consecutive samples of each kind
    while len(expressions) < self.num_expressions:
        # unique=False: uniqueness is checked below, across batches and after the constraint filter.
        batch = generate_n_expressions(
            grammar,
            max(self.num_expressions - len(expressions), 64),
            unique=False,
            max_expression_length=self.max_expression_length,
            verbose=False,
        )
        for expr in batch:
            # The HVAE's vocabulary has only the library's symbols, so labelled constants become bare.
            expr = [constant if (s := symbol_library.get(t)) is not None and s.type == "const" else t for t in expr]
            if any(r.implemented and not r.passed for r in (c.pre_check(expr) for c in required_constraints)):
                rejected += 1
                if rejected >= self.max_training_skips:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"[EDHiE] {rejected} sampled expressions in a row broke a required constraint; "
                        "the grammar cannot produce valid training expressions."
                    )
                continue
            rejected = 0
            key = "".join(expr)
            if not allow_repeats and key in seen:
                repeats += 1
                if repeats >= self.max_training_skips:
                    allow_repeats = True
                    warnings.warn(
                        f"[EDHiE] Only {len(expressions)} distinct valid training expressions found; "
                        f"filling the remaining {self.num_expressions - len(expressions)} with repeats."
                    )
                continue
            repeats = 0
            seen.add(key)
            expressions.append(expr)
            if len(expressions) == self.num_expressions:
                break
    return expressions

def save_adapted_state(self, path: str) -> None:
    """Save the HVAE (architecture, symbol library and weights) to ``path``.

    Args:

def start(self, evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> _GASearch:
    """Seed the random states and start a new search.

    See [start][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.start]. With ``seed`` set, it seeds the global
    random states (Python, NumPy, PyTorch; not restored) and the GA's own generator, so the same
    seed, HVAE, approach and evaluator settings give the same run; with ``None``, the GA's
    generator draws fresh entropy.

        seed: The run's seed, or ``None``.

  2. a skip "evaluated" if skip_evaluated is set and its stored form (see stored_tokens) is that of an expression evaluated before or proposed for evaluation earlier in this generation;
  3. a skip "rejected" if skip_rejected is set and it breaks a required constraint;
  4. its expression, to be evaluated.

def ask(self, evaluator: Evaluator, state: _GASearch) -> list[Candidate | list[str] | Expression | None]:
    """Decode the next generation and propose one entry per individual, in order.

    See [ask][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.ask]. Each individual is proposed as the first of
    these that applies:

    1. ``None`` if it does not decode;
    2. a skip ``"evaluated"`` if ``skip_evaluated`` is set and its stored form (see
       [stored_tokens][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.stored_tokens]) is that of
       an expression evaluated before or proposed for evaluation earlier in this generation;
    3. a skip ``"rejected"`` if ``skip_rejected`` is set and it breaks a required constraint;
    4. its expression, to be evaluated.

    Args:
        evaluator: The evaluator of the run.
        state: The search state.

    Returns:
        One entry per individual; never empty.
    """
    assert self.model is not None  # checked by start and load_search_state
    state.pending = state.ga.ask()
    X = state.pending.get("X")
    device = next(self.model.parameters()).device
    trees = self.model.decode(torch.tensor(X, device=device, dtype=torch.float32))
    candidates: list[Candidate | list[str] | Expression | None] = []
    evaluated: set[tuple[str, ...]] = set()  # stored forms of the expressions proposed for evaluation
    for tree in trees:
        if tree is None:  # Shouldn't happen but just to be safe
            candidates.append(None)
            continue
        # One Expression per individual, so the lookups below and the evaluation parse it once.
        expr = Expression.from_tree(tree, evaluator.symbol_library)
        key = tuple(evaluator.stored_tokens(expr))
        if self.skip_evaluated and (key in evaluated or evaluator.get_model(expr) is not None):
            candidates.append(Candidate(expr, skip="evaluated"))
        elif self.skip_rejected and evaluator.check_constraints(expr)[0]:
            candidates.append(Candidate(expr, skip="rejected"))
        else:
            candidates.append(expr)
            evaluated.add(key)
    return candidates

def tell(
    self,
    evaluator: Evaluator,
    state: _GASearch,
    candidates: list[Candidate | list[str] | Expression | None],
    results: "list[ModelResult | None]",
) -> None:
    """Score the generation from ``ask`` and select the next population.

    See [tell][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.tell]. Individual *i* gets the error of
    ``results[i]`` (lower is better), or ``inf`` if that is ``None``, its error is ``nan``, or
    the step stopped before it.

    Args:
        evaluator: The evaluator of the run.
        state: The search state.
        candidates: Not used.
        results: The models of the entries from ``ask`` that the step loop reached.
    """
    assert state.pending is not None  # set by ask
    errors = np.full(len(state.pending), np.inf)
    for i, result in enumerate(results):
        if result is not None and not np.isnan(result.error):
            errors[i] = result.error
    state.pending.set("F", errors[:, None])
    state.ga.tell(infills=state.pending)
    state.pending = None

def dump_search_state(self, state: _GASearch) -> bytes:
    """Serialise the search state between two steps.

    See [dump_search_state][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.dump_search_state].

    Args:
        state: The search state.

    Returns:
        The search state without the HVAE; only a fingerprint of the HVAE is saved, and
        ``load_search_state`` checks it.
    """
    assert self.model is not None  # checked by start and load_search_state
    # The GA itself does not pickle (tournament selection holds a local function); mating is
    # configuration only and the problem holds the HVAE, so both are rebuilt on load.
    ga = {k: v for k, v in vars(state.ga).items() if k not in ("mating", "problem")}
    return pickle.dumps({"ga": ga, "model": _digest(self.model)})

def load_search_state(self, data: bytes) -> _GASearch:
    """Rebuild a search state from ``dump_search_state``, on this approach's HVAE.

    See [load_search_state][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.load_search_state].

    Args:
        data: The serialised state.

    Returns:
        The search state, with the dumped GA settings.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If there is no HVAE (no ``adapt`` and no ``weights_path``).
        ValueError: If the HVAE differs from the one the state was saved with (state dicts
            compared bit for bit).
    """
    if self.model is None:
        raise RuntimeError("EDHiE needs an HVAE to restore a search state: call adapt() or pass weights_path.")
    saved = pickle.loads(data)
    if saved["model"] != _digest(self.model):
        raise ValueError(
            "EDHiE: the HVAE differs from the one the search state was saved with (weights must match "
            "bit for bit); load the same model (weights_path or a saved adapted state) or train it with "
            "the same training_seed on the same device and PyTorch version."
        )
    ga = self._new_ga(None)
    vars(ga).update(saved["ga"])
    return _GASearch(ga)

ProGED(grammar: str | Grammar | SymbolLibrary | None = None, skip_evaluated: bool = True, skip_rejected: bool = True)

Bases: Approach

Random sampling from a probabilistic context-free grammar (a slimmed-down ProGED).

The grammar's rule weights bias sampling toward likely expressions and its registered GrammarConstraints exclude invalid ones; a domain-specific grammar is how this approach uses prior knowledge. Full version: https://github.com/brencej/ProGED.

Each step of the step interface proposes one sample, and a stopped run can be resumed. Resuming needs the same grammar (the same constructor argument, or the same task for adapt); a different one is not detected.

References

Brence et al. (2021)

Examples:

>>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
>>> dataset = Feynman().create_dataset('I.16.6')
>>> dataset.max_evaluations = 100
>>> results = dataset.evaluate_approach(ProGED(), num_experiments=1, initial_seed=19, verbose=False)
>>> results[0].best_expr
'C-X_0/C-X_0'

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default grammar str | Grammar | SymbolLibrary | None

Grammar to sample from: a Grammar, a string for Grammar.from_grammar_string, a SymbolLibrary (converted with Grammar.from_symbol_library), or None to let adapt choose one per task. Sample length is bounded only by the derivation limit of ask; a MaxTokens required constraint rejects long samples. For a grammar with labelled constants as terminals, the evaluator setting evaluator.canonicalise_constants (see EvaluatorSettings) treats samples that differ only in constant labels (C_0*X_0 + C_0 and C_1*X_0 + C_1) as one expression, so they count as repeats for skip_evaluated.

None skip_evaluated bool

Skip samples that were already evaluated (see ask). False evaluates repeats too, as cache hits that use the budget.

True skip_rejected bool

Skip samples that break a required constraint. False evaluates them, so they use the budget and appear in the results as "rejected".

def __init__(
    self,
    grammar: str | Grammar | SymbolLibrary | None = None,
    skip_evaluated: bool = True,
    skip_rejected: bool = True,
) -> None:
    r"""Random sampling from a probabilistic context-free grammar (a slimmed-down ProGED).

    The grammar's rule weights bias sampling toward likely expressions and its registered
    [GrammarConstraint][SRToolkit.utils.grammar.GrammarConstraint]s exclude invalid ones; a
    domain-specific grammar is how this approach uses prior knowledge. Full version:
    https://github.com/brencej/ProGED.

    Each step of the [step interface][SRToolkit.approaches.approach] proposes one sample, and
    a stopped run can be resumed. Resuming needs the same grammar (the same constructor
    argument, or the same task for ``adapt``); a different one is not detected.

    References:
        [Brence et al. (2021)][cite-proged]

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> dataset = Feynman().create_dataset('I.16.6')
        >>> dataset.max_evaluations = 100
        >>> results = dataset.evaluate_approach(ProGED(), num_experiments=1, initial_seed=19, verbose=False)
        >>> results[0].best_expr
        'C-X_0/C-X_0'

    Args:
        grammar: Grammar to sample from: a [Grammar][SRToolkit.utils.grammar.Grammar], a string
            for [Grammar.from_grammar_string][SRToolkit.utils.grammar.Grammar.from_grammar_string],
            a [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary] (converted with
            [Grammar.from_symbol_library][SRToolkit.utils.grammar.Grammar.from_symbol_library]),
            or ``None`` to let [adapt][SRToolkit.approaches.ProGED.ProGED.adapt] choose one per
            task. Sample length is bounded only by the derivation limit of
            [ask][SRToolkit.approaches.ProGED.ProGED.ask]; a ``MaxTokens`` required constraint
            rejects long samples. For a grammar with labelled constants as terminals, the
            evaluator setting ``evaluator.canonicalise_constants`` (see
            [EvaluatorSettings][SRToolkit.utils.settings.EvaluatorSettings]) treats samples that differ
            only in constant labels (``C_0*X_0 + C_0`` and ``C_1*X_0 + C_1``) as one expression,
            so they count as repeats for ``skip_evaluated``.
        skip_evaluated: Skip samples that were already evaluated (see
            [ask][SRToolkit.approaches.ProGED.ProGED.ask]). ``False`` evaluates repeats too, as
            cache hits that use the budget.
        skip_rejected: Skip samples that break a required constraint. ``False`` evaluates them,
            so they use the budget and appear in the results as ``"rejected"``.
    """
    if isinstance(grammar, Grammar):
        grammar_dict = grammar.to_dict()
    elif isinstance(grammar, SymbolLibrary):
        grammar = Grammar.from_symbol_library(grammar)
        grammar_dict = grammar.to_dict()
    elif isinstance(grammar, str):
        grammar = Grammar.from_grammar_string(grammar)
        grammar_dict = grammar.to_dict()
    else:
        grammar = None
        grammar_dict = None
    super().__init__(
        ProGEDConfig(
            grammar=grammar_dict,
            skip_evaluated=skip_evaluated,
            skip_rejected=skip_rejected,
        )
    )
    self.grammar: Grammar | None = grammar
    self.skip_evaluated = skip_evaluated
    self.skip_rejected = skip_rejected
    # The grammar search samples from: the constructor's, or the one adapt chose for this task.
    self._sampling_grammar: Grammar | None = grammar

Propose one sample from the grammar.

A derivation that needs more than 1000 rule applications, or in which no rule fits, fails and is proposed as None (the skip "not_expression"), not redrawn. A sample is proposed with the skip reason "evaluated" if skip_evaluated is set and its stored form was evaluated before (see get_model), else "rejected" if skip_rejected is set and it breaks a required constraint.

Source code in SRToolkit/approaches/ProGED.py 
def ask(self, evaluator: Evaluator, state: None) -> list[Candidate | list[str] | Expression | None]:
    """Propose one sample from the grammar.

    A derivation that needs more than 1000 rule applications, or in which no rule fits, fails
    and is proposed as ``None`` (the skip ``"not_expression"``), not redrawn. A sample is
    proposed with the skip reason ``"evaluated"`` if ``skip_evaluated`` is set and its stored
    form was evaluated before (see
    [get_model][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.get_model]), else
    ``"rejected"`` if ``skip_rejected`` is set and it breaks a required constraint.

    Returns:
        A one-element list: a [Candidate][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Candidate], or
        ``None`` if the derivation failed.
    """
    assert self._sampling_grammar is not None  # set by the constructor or adapt; checked in start
    tokens = self._sampling_grammar.generate_one(max_retries=1)
    if tokens is None:
        return [None]
    # One Expression, so the lookups below and the evaluation parse it once.
    expr = Expression(tokens, evaluator.symbol_library)
    if self.skip_evaluated and evaluator.get_model(expr) is not None:
        return [Candidate(expr, skip="evaluated")]
    if self.skip_rejected and evaluator.check_constraints(expr)[0]:
        return [Candidate(expr, skip="rejected")]
    return [Candidate(expr)]

docs.title: SRToolkit.approaches.approach
docs.text: Base class and configuration of symbolic regression approaches.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
One approach object can run many experiments. Each part of it sets up one kind of state:

  • __init__: the hyperparameters, from the config.
  • adapt: what the task alone determines, e.g. a grammar for its symbol library or a trained model; how often it runs is set by adaptation_scope. A resumed run adapts again or loads the adapted state.
  • the search: everything a run learns. The search does not change the approach object, so one run cannot leak into the next: a step approach keeps what it learns in the state start returns, an approach with its own search in that call's local variables.

docs.title: Two ways to implement the search
docs.text:
An approach implements either search, its own loop that calls evaluate_expr until should_stop, or the step interface, in which the framework runs the loop:

  • start(se, seed) seeds the random generators and returns a new search state (e.g. no population yet);
  • ask(se, state) proposes the next expressions: the first call creates them from scratch (e.g. a random population), later ones build on what tell stored;
  • tell(se, state, candidates, results) updates the state in place from their ModelResults (e.g. selects the next population); an approach that learns nothing from the results (e.g. random sampling) doesn't need to implement it;
  • dump_search_state and load_search_state save and restore the state between two steps; they pickle it by default.

The state is any object ask and tell can change in place, or None if the search keeps nothing. The framework passes the same object to every ask, tell and dump_search_state call of a session (one run call, new or resumed) and never replaces it. A step approach does not also override search: a resumed run continues the step loop without calling it.

One step is one ask, the evaluation of its candidates and one tell. What it covers (one sample, a batch, a generation of a genetic algorithm) is the approach's choice; document it. Only the framework evaluates: start, ask and tell never call evaluate_expr, so every evaluation falls in a step, which an interrupt lets finish and a snapshot never splits.

docs.title: Which one to implement
docs.text:
search is the simpler choice: write the loop as you would anyway, or call a library that runs its own. Its runs write checkpoints like any other, so their results survive a crash, but a stopped run starts again from the beginning.

The step interface takes more work, since the search state is passed between calls. In return, a stopped or crashed run continues from its last snapshot and finds the same models as a run that was never stopped (see Checkpoints), provided ask and tell depend only on the state, the adapted approach object and the global random states (Python, NumPy, PyTorch), which the framework saves. A random generator of the approach's own (e.g. a numpy.random.Generator) therefore belongs in the state, not on the object.

docs.title: The step loop
docs.text:
For a step approach, the framework runs this loop (this is what the inherited search does). An approach that overrides search runs its own loop instead, and start, ask and tell are never called. snapshots is true when the evaluator has a checkpoint:

state = approach.start(se, seed)
if snapshots:
    approach.dump_search_state(state)  # fails early if the state cannot be saved
stepped, complete = False, True
while not se.should_stop:
    stepped = True
    if snapshots and se.snapshot_due:
        se.save_snapshot(approach.dump_search_state(state))
    candidates = approach.ask(se, state)
    if not candidates:
        break  # as if search had returned
    with se.step():
        results = []
        for candidate in candidates:
            if se.should_stop:
                break
            if candidate is None:  # not an expression: neither looked up nor evaluated
                results.append(None)
                se.count_skip("not_expression")
                continue
            if not isinstance(candidate, Candidate):  # a token list or an Expression
                candidate = Candidate(candidate)
            if candidate.skip is None:
                results.append(se.evaluate_expr(candidate.expr))
            else:  # a skip: looked up without spending budget (None if never evaluated) and counted
                results.append(se.get_model(candidate.expr))
                se.count_skip(candidate.skip)
    approach.tell(se, state, candidates[: len(results)], results)
    complete = len(results) == len(candidates)
if snapshots and stepped and complete:  # when the loop ends normally, unless its last step was cut
    se.save_snapshot(approach.dump_search_state(state))

Snapshots fall between steps, where nothing is half done. None is taken after an exception; after a step that a stop cut short (its tell saw only part of its results), so that an extended run redoes that step in full; or at the end of a session in which should_stop was already true (e.g. a finished run resumed), which keeps the snapshot it has. run continues this loop from the evaluator's snapshot when resuming, with state = approach.load_search_state(snapshot.state) (followed by restoring the global random states) in place of start, and calls search otherwise.

docs.title: Skips
docs.text:
A skip is an expression the approach discards without evaluating it. Skips are counted by reason (see count_skip), and the run stops after the setting evaluator.max_consecutive_skips of them in a row (an evaluate_expr call resets the count).

A step approach reports a skip through its proposals, and the loop above counts them in order:

  • a candidate with a skip reason, e.g. Candidate(expr, skip="rejected") (see Candidate): it is looked up instead of evaluated, so tell still gets its model if it was evaluated before;
  • None for something that is not an expression, counted as "not_expression".

Calling count_skip from ask instead counts the skip before the step's candidates run, so it can stop the run before any of them is evaluated. Prefer proposing the expression as a skip.

ApproachConfig(name: str = 'base', approach_class: str = '')

Serialisable base configuration for SR approaches.

Subclass this dataclass to define approach-specific hyperparameters that can be saved and restored via to_dict and from_dict. Fields must hold values that can be saved (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, numpy arrays, …; see serialization).

The approach_class field is populated automatically by Approach and contains the fully-qualified importlib path of the concrete approach class. This makes a serialised config dict self-sufficient for reconstruction without any additional metadata.

Examples:

>>> cfg = ApproachConfig(name="my_approach")
>>> d = cfg.to_dict()
>>> ApproachConfig.from_dict(d).name

search(evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> None

Run the search of one experiment.

The default runs the step interface: start, then the step loop shown in the module docs. Approaches without the step interface override it, keeping the search state in local variables (see the lifecycle in the module docs). Score expressions with evaluate_expr; the framework collects the results. evaluate_expr returns the expression's ModelResult, with its error, fitted parameters and status.

Search while evaluator.should_stop is False; it turns True when the success threshold or the budget is reached, a callback stops the run, or the run is interrupted (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM). To end the search early (e.g. the search space is exhausted), call evaluator.stop with a reason, so the results explain why; returning without it is recorded as "returned".

The symbol library is available in evaluator.symbol_library. evaluator.describe() gives the task as text (e.g. for an LLM prompt) and evaluator.background_knowledge as objects. Do not read evaluator.ground_truth: it is the answer. Report expressions discarded without evaluation as skips (see Skips).

def search(self, evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> None:
    """Run the search of one experiment.

    The default runs the step interface: ``start``, then the step loop shown in the
    [module docs][SRToolkit.approaches.approach]. Approaches without the step interface
    override it, keeping the search state in local variables (see the lifecycle in the module
    docs). Score expressions with ``evaluate_expr``; the framework collects the results.
    ``evaluate_expr`` returns the expression's
    [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult], with its error, fitted ``parameters``
    and ``status``.

    Search while ``evaluator.should_stop`` is ``False``; it turns ``True`` when the success
    threshold or the budget is reached, a callback stops the run, or the run is interrupted
    (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM). To end the search early (e.g. the search space is exhausted), call
    [evaluator.stop][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.stop] with a reason, so
    the results explain why; returning without it is recorded as ``"returned"``.

    The symbol library is available in ``evaluator.symbol_library``. ``evaluator.describe()``
    gives the task as text (e.g. for an LLM prompt) and ``evaluator.background_knowledge`` as
    objects. Do not read ``evaluator.ground_truth``: it is the answer. Report expressions
    discarded without evaluation as skips (see [Skips][SRToolkit.approaches.approach]).

    Args:
        evaluator: Evaluator used to score expressions. All results are
            stored inside this object.
        seed: Optional random seed for reproducible expression generation.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If the approach implements neither ``search`` nor ``ask``, or
            implements ``ask`` without ``start``.
    """
    if not self.supports_steps:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"[{type(self).__name__}] implements neither search() nor the step interface (start/ask/tell)."
        )
    self._step_loop(evaluator, self.start(evaluator, seed))

def run(self, evaluator: Evaluator, seed: int | None = None) -> None:
    """Run the approach on ``evaluator``: continue from its snapshot, or search anew.

    If ``evaluator.resumed_from`` holds a
    [Snapshot][SRToolkit.evaluation.model_store.Snapshot], the search state is restored with
    [load_search_state][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.load_search_state], then
    the global random states, and the step loop continues; neither ``start`` nor ``search`` is
    called, and errors of ``load_search_state`` propagate. Otherwise it calls [search][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.search]. If the
    search returns while evaluation goes on, ``run`` stops it with the reason ``"returned"``,
    so the checkpoint records the run as finished.
    [evaluate_approach][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.evaluate_approach] and
    [ExperimentJob.run][SRToolkit.experiments.ExperimentJob.run] call it.

    Args:
        evaluator: The evaluator, new or resumed.
        seed: The seed passed to ``search`` for a new run; ignored when continuing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the evaluator holds a snapshot but the approach lacks the step
            interface.
    """
    snapshot = evaluator.resumed_from
    if snapshot is None:
        self.search(evaluator, seed)
    else:
        if not self.supports_steps:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[{type(self).__name__}] cannot continue from a snapshot: it lacks the step interface "
                "(start/ask/tell)."
            )
        state = self.load_search_state(snapshot.state)
        _restore_rngs(snapshot.rngs)
        self._step_loop(evaluator, state)
    if not evaluator.should_stop:
        evaluator.stop("returned")

def dump_search_state(self, state: Any) -> bytes:
    """Serialise the search state for a snapshot (step interface).

    Called between steps when a snapshot is due, when the loop ends, and, with a checkpoint,
    once before the first step of every session (new or resumed) with the result discarded, so a state that cannot be saved fails
    before any budget is spent. It must not change ``state``: the run continues with it. The
    default pickles it and raises whatever ``pickle`` raises if the state does not pickle;
    override it then, or to leave out what ``load_search_state`` can rebuild. The state must
    include the approach's own random generators and anything the search fine-tunes (e.g.

def from_config_dict(cls, config: dict) -> "Approach":
    """Reconstruct an approach from a config dict that includes an ``approach_class`` path.

    This is the self-dispatching counterpart to
    [from_config][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.from_config]: it binds the
    config to any installed ``.srtk`` bundle, resolves the concrete approach class named
    by ``approach_class``, and delegates to that class's
    [from_config][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.from_config]. Mirrors
    [Dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.from_dict], which
    resolves its own class the same way.

    Args:

            produced by

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``approach_class`` cannot be imported (e.g. its ``.srtk`` bundle
            is not installed, or the config has no ``_bundle`` key and was never bound).
        TypeError: If ``approach_class`` is not an Approach subclass.

    target_cls = _import_class(config["approach_class"], "approach", Approach)

docs.title: SRToolkit.bundle
docs.text:
Bundle sharing utilities for the Symbolic Regression Toolkit.

Provides tools for packing, installing, and using bundles of user-defined Python code as .srtk archives. Bundles contain code only — configs (the settings a user chose) are intentionally separate so they can be shared, versioned, and tweaked independently of the implementation.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Author side — pack the code:

from SRToolkit.bundle import pack

pack(
    files=["my_approach/approach.py", "my_approach/ops.py"],
    out_path="meznar_gp.srtk",
    name="meznar-gp",
    version="0.1.0",
    author="meznar",
    python_deps=["torch>=2.0"],
)

Share the .srtk file and a plain JSON config separately.

Recipient side — install and use:

import json
from SRToolkit.bundle import install

install("meznar_gp.srtk")   # one-time, interactive

raw = json.load(open("meznar_settings.srtk.json"))  # config shared separately
# The config is annotated with _bundle/_version by pack(..., configs=[...]),
# so it can be passed straight to any project `from_dict` consumer
# (Dataset, Sampler, the experiment grid, ...) — they call bind_config
# internally to repoint every *_class path at the installed bundle.
benchmark = Benchmark.from_dict(raw)

If the config was not annotated by pack (no _bundle key), bind it explicitly first, passing the bundle name:

from SRToolkit.bundle import bind_config

config = bind_config(raw, "meznar-gp")

Listing and removing:

from SRToolkit.bundle import list_installed, uninstall

for entry in list_installed():
    print(entry["name"], entry["version"])

uninstall("meznar-gp", version="0.1.0")

Install a .srtk bundle onto this machine.

Steps:

  1. Unzip to a temporary directory and load the manifest.
  2. Verify per-file checksums declared in the manifest.
  3. Check the required SRToolkit version.
  4. Check Python dependencies — list missing ones and suggest a pip install command; the user decides whether to continue.
  5. Prompt the user to confirm that arbitrary user code will be executable.
  6. Copy src/ to the managed bundle directory.
  7. Register the bundle in the local index.

def install(srtk_path: Path) -> None:
    """Install a ``.srtk`` bundle onto this machine.

    Steps:

    1. Unzip to a temporary directory and load the manifest.
    2. Verify per-file checksums declared in the manifest.
    3. Check the required ``SRToolkit`` version.
    4. Check Python dependencies — list missing ones and suggest a ``pip install``
       command; the user decides whether to continue.
    5. Prompt the user to confirm that arbitrary user code will be executable.
    6. Copy ``src/`` to the managed bundle directory.
    7. Register the bundle in the local index.

    Args:
        srtk_path: Path to a ``.srtk`` bundle file produced by
            [pack][SRToolkit.bundle.pack].

    Raises:
        ValueError: On checksum mismatch.
        RuntimeError: If the installed SRToolkit is too old.
    """
    srtk_path = Path(srtk_path)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp_dir = Path(tmp)
        manifest = _extract_and_verify(srtk_path, tmp_dir)

        missing_deps = _check_deps(manifest.python_deps)
        if missing_deps:
            print(f"Bundle '{manifest.name}' declares missing dependencies:")
            for dep in missing_deps:
                print(f"  {dep}")
            print(f"\nInstall them with:\n  pip install {' '.join(missing_deps)}\n")
            if not _confirm("Continue installation without them?"):
                print("Installation cancelled.")
                return

        print(
            f"\nBundle '{manifest.name}' v{manifest.version}"
            + (f" by {manifest.author!r}" if manifest.author else "")
            + " contains user-defined code that will run when loaded."
        )
        if not _confirm("Install?"):
            print("Installation cancelled.")
            return

        install_path = _store.bundle_path(manifest.name, manifest.version)
        if install_path.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(install_path)
        install_path.mkdir(parents=True)

        src_tmp = tmp_dir / "src"
        if src_tmp.exists():
            shutil.copytree(src_tmp, install_path, dirs_exist_ok=True)

        _store.register(manifest, install_path)
        _store.enable_bundle_imports()
        print(f"Installed '{manifest.name}' v{manifest.version} → {install_path}")

def read_manifest(srtk_path: Path) -> BundleManifest:
    """Read a ``.srtk`` bundle's manifest without installing it.

    Reads only the ``manifest.json`` entry from the archive — the bundle's source files
    are not extracted, no checksums are verified, and the global bundle store is not
    touched. Use this to inspect a not-yet-installed bundle's ``name`` / ``version`` /
    ``import_prefix`` (e.g. to match referenced class paths against a bundle a user
    supplied to [share.save][SRToolkit.share.save]).

    Args:
        srtk_path: Path to the ``.srtk`` archive.

    Returns:
        The bundle's [BundleManifest][SRToolkit.bundle._manifest.BundleManifest].

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If ``srtk_path`` does not exist.
        ValueError: If the archive is not a valid bundle (no ``manifest.json``).
    """
    srtk_path = Path(srtk_path)
    if not srtk_path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No bundle archive at {str(srtk_path)!r}.")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(srtk_path) as zf:
            raw = zf.read("manifest.json")
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"{str(srtk_path)!r} is not a valid .srtk bundle (no manifest.json).") from exc
    return BundleManifest.from_dict(json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8")))

def uninstall(name: str, version: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Remove an installed bundle from this machine.

    Args:
        name: Bundle name.
        version: Version to remove. If ``None``, removes the latest installed version.
    """
    entry = _store.lookup(name, version)
    install_path = Path(entry["path"])
    if install_path.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(install_path)
    _store.deregister(entry["name"], entry["version"])
    print(f"Uninstalled '{entry['name']}' v{entry['version']}")

Each file is stored flat under src/ using its basename, so all filenames must be unique. Configs are intentionally excluded from the archive — share them separately as plain JSON. Class paths are rewritten at use-time by calling bind_config.

The archive layout is::

    must be unique. Configs are intentionally excluded from the archive — share
    them separately as plain JSON. Class paths are rewritten at use-time by
    calling [bind_config][SRToolkit.bundle.bind_config].

    If ``configs`` is provided, each JSON config file is annotated with
    ``_bundle`` and ``_version`` metadata and written next to the original with
    a ``.srtk.json`` suffix (e.g. ``settings.json`` → ``settings.srtk.json``).
    These annotated copies are the files to share alongside the ``.srtk`` bundle;
    the originals are left untouched.

    The archive layout is::

        manifest.json
        src/
            <basename of each file>

    Args:
        files: Paths to the ``.py`` files to include. Basenames must be unique.
        out_path: Destination path for the ``.srtk`` file (created or overwritten).
        name: Bundle name (alphanumeric, hyphens allowed).
        version: Semantic version string, e.g. ``"0.2.1"``.
        author: Optional author identifier.
        python_deps: List of PEP 508 dependency specifiers, e.g. ``["torch>=2.0"]``.
        srtk_min_version: Minimum ``SRToolkit`` version required to run this bundle.
        configs: Optional list of JSON config file paths to annotate. Each is
            written to ``<stem>.srtk.json`` in the same directory.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If any source or config file does not exist.
        ValueError: If a source file is not ``.py``, two source files share the
            same basename, or a config already contains ``_bundle`` or
            ``_version`` keys (indicates an already-annotated config).
    """
    out_path = Path(out_path)
    python_deps = python_deps or []

    resolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    seen_basenames: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for raw in files:
        p = Path(raw).resolve()
        if not p.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {p}")
        if p.suffix != ".py":
            raise ValueError(f"Only .py files are supported: {p}")
        if p.name in seen_basenames:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate basename {p.name!r}: {seen_basenames[p.name]} and {p}")
        seen_basenames[p.name] = p
        resolved.append((p, f"src/{p.name}"))

    archive_files: dict[str, str] = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(out_path, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for file_path, archive_name in resolved:
            zf.write(file_path, archive_name)
            archive_files[archive_name] = _sha256(file_path)

        manifest = BundleManifest(
            name=name,
            version=version,
            author=author,
            srtk_min_version=srtk_min_version,
            python_deps=python_deps,
            files=archive_files,
        )
        zf.writestr("manifest.json", json.dumps(manifest.to_dict(), indent=2))

    if configs:
        for cfg_raw in configs:
            cfg_path = Path(cfg_raw).resolve()
            if not cfg_path.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config file not found: {cfg_path}")
            cfg = json.loads(cfg_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if "_bundle" in cfg or "_version" in cfg:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{cfg_path.name} already contains '_bundle' or '_version' — "
                    "pass the original config, not an already-annotated one."
                )
            annotated = {"_bundle": name, "_version": version, **cfg}
            out = cfg_path.parent / (cfg_path.stem + ".srtk.json")
            out.write_text(json.dumps(annotated, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

def bind_config(
    config: dict,
    bundle_name: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Rewrite ``*_class`` paths in ``config`` to point at an installed bundle.

    Looks up ``bundle_name`` in the local bundle index and rewrites every
    ``*_class`` value so that it resolves to the installed copy's import prefix.
    Paths already starting with ``SRToolkit.`` are left unchanged.

    If ``bundle_name`` is not provided, the ``_bundle`` and ``_version`` keys
    embedded in the config by [pack][SRToolkit.bundle.pack] are used as
    fallbacks. This allows calling ``bind_config(config)`` directly when the
    config was annotated at pack time.

    This is the recipient-side complement to [pack][SRToolkit.bundle.pack] for configs:
    the author shares the ``.srtk`` file (code) and an annotated ``.srtk.json``
    config; the recipient installs the bundle once and then calls ``bind_config``
    to make the config usable on their machine.

    Args:
        config: JSON-style configuration dictionary, optionally containing
            ``_bundle`` and ``_version`` metadata added by ``pack``.
        bundle_name: Name of an installed bundle. If ``None``, ``config["_bundle"]``
            is used.
        version: Version to bind against. If ``None``, ``config["_version"]`` is
            tried first, then the latest installed version.

    Returns:
        A new dictionary with rewritten ``*_class`` references ready for use
        with ``from_dict`` dispatchers. ``config`` is not modified and ``_bundle``/
        ``_version`` metadata keys are stripped from the result.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``bundle_name`` is not provided and ``config`` has no
            ``_bundle`` key.
        KeyError: If the bundle (or requested version) is not installed.
        LookupError: If a ``*_class`` value references a class that cannot be
            found in the installed bundle.
    """
    resolved_name = bundle_name or config.get("_bundle")
    if not resolved_name:
        raise ValueError(
            "bundle_name must be provided or the config must contain a '_bundle' key "
            "(added automatically by pack(..., configs=[...]))."
        )
    resolved_version = version or config.get("_version")

    entry = _store.lookup(resolved_name, resolved_version)
    _store.enable_bundle_imports()

    stripped = {k: v for k, v in config.items() if k not in ("_bundle", "_version")}
    return _relocate_class_paths(stripped, entry["import_prefix"], entry["path"])

def enable_bundle_imports() -> None:
    """Make installed bundles importable in the current Python process.

    Adds the bundles-root parent directory to ``sys.path`` (if not already
    present) so that ``import srtk_bundles.<safe_name>_<version_slug>`` works.
    Idempotent and safe to call repeatedly.

    Called automatically at the end of [install][SRToolkit.bundle.install] and
    by [bind_config][SRToolkit.bundle.bind_config]. Call it directly only when
    you want to ``import`` a bundle's classes by hand in a fresh Python session
    without going through ``from_dict`` / ``bind_config``.
    """
    bundles_parent = str(bundles_root().parent)
    if bundles_parent not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, bundles_parent)

def verify(self, extracted_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if any declared file is missing or has a wrong checksum."""
    for rel, expected in self.files.items():
        p = extracted_dir / rel
        if not p.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"Bundle file missing: {rel}")
        actual = _sha256(p)
        if actual != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"Checksum mismatch for {rel}: expected {expected[:12]}…, got {actual[:12]}…")

docs.title: SRToolkit.dataset
docs.text:
Datasets and benchmarks for symbolic regression.

A dataset (Dataset) represents a single equation with associated data, a symbol library, and evaluation constraints. A benchmark (Benchmark) is a collection of datasets.

Modules:

Name Description dataset

Dataset — wraps input data and evaluation settings for a single equation discovery problem.

background_knowledge

BackgroundKnowledge and VariableInfo — what a dataset tells the approach besides the data (symbols, input distribution, hints, descriptions).

benchmark

Benchmark — manages a collection of datasets.

feynman

Feynman — 100-equation physics benchmark.

nguyen

Nguyen — 10-equation polynomial/trig benchmark.

srsd_feynman

SRSD_Feynman — 120-equation SRSD physics benchmark with per-variable sampling strategies.

sampling

LogUniformSampling, UniformSampling, IntegerUniformSampling — variable samplers with serialisation support.

data_source

DataSource and its concrete types UrlSource and SampleSource — describe where a dataset's cached data originates.

data_split

DataSplit — named arrays (e.g. a dataset's held-out test data) with an optional data source.

data_cache

dataset cache management — list, gc, remove, refresh, dataset_path — plus the materialisation engine used internally by the dataset machinery.

BackgroundKnowledge(symbol_library: SymbolLibrary, samplers: Mapping[str, Sampler] | Sequence[Sampler] | None = None, constant_bounds: tuple[float, float] = (-5.0, 5.0), constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] = (), reference_grammar: Grammar | None = None, description: str = '', variables: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] = dict(), target: VariableInfo | None = None, named_constants: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] = dict(), default_constant: Constant | None = None)

Everything a dataset tells the approach besides the data, without the answer.

See the module docstring for what belongs here and what does not.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default symbol_library SymbolLibrary

The tokens expressions may use.

required samplers Mapping[str, Sampler] | Sequence[Sampler] | None

One Sampler per variable of symbol_library, as a mapping {token: sampler} or a list in the library's variable order (the column order of X). None if not given.

None constant_bounds tuple[float, float]

(lower, upper) range of the default spec when default_constant is None (uniform_default(constant_bounds)); also fills the unset prior or bounds of default_constant. Finite, with lower < upper; validated even when default_constant sets both. Defaults to (-5, 5).

(-5.0, 5.0) constraints Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]

Advisory constraints (hints).

() reference_grammar Grammar | None

A grammar an approach may start from. Its terminal tokens must be symbols of symbol_library, brackets or numbers.

None description str

Free text, as a domain expert would write it: what was measured, under which conditions, and what is known about the phenomenon (signs, limiting cases, monotonicity, symmetries). Must not name the law or equation being discovered.

'' variables Mapping[str, VariableInfo]

Information per variable, keyed by the variable's token in symbol_library (e.g. "X_0"). Variables may be left out.

dict() target VariableInfo | None

Information about the target, or None.

None named_constants Mapping[str, VariableInfo]

Information per named constant, keyed by the constant's token, which must be a symbol of type "lit" in symbol_library (e.g. "c" for the speed of light). Named constants may be left out.

dict() default_constant Constant | None

The default spec for free constants without a spec of their own: a Constant without label or value, e.g. Constant(prior=LogUniformSampling(0.1, 10), bounds=(0, float("inf"))). Its unset prior or bounds come from uniform_default(constant_bounds), so set both for a prior that matches the bounds. None: uniform_default(constant_bounds).

None

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If an argument has the wrong type, e.g. a lone constraint or a string as constraints, a constant_bounds that is not a pair of real numbers (bool is not accepted), or a default_constant that is not a Constant.

ValueError

If samplers does not give exactly one sampler per variable (the message names missing or unknown tokens); constant_bounds is not finite with lower < upper; default_constant has a label, a value or fixed=True; a key of variables is not a variable of symbol_library, or a key of named_constants is not one of its "lit" symbols; a constraint does not fit symbol_library (raised by its setup); or reference_grammar has a terminal token that is not a symbol, bracket or number (the message names it). Errors about constant_bounds or default_constant name the argument in the message.

Attributes:

Name Type Description symbol_library SymbolLibrary

The symbol library, as given.

samplers Mapping[str, Sampler] | Sequence[Sampler] | None

The samplers as a tuple in the library's variable order, or None.

constant_bounds tuple[float, float]

(lower, upper) as a tuple of two floats.

default_constant Constant | None

The default spec, complete (prior and bounds set).

constraints Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]

The advisory constraints, as a tuple.

reference_grammar Grammar | None

The grammar, as given, or None.

description str

The description, as given.

variables Mapping[str, VariableInfo]

A copy of variables as a dict from token to VariableInfo, in the library's variable order.

target VariableInfo | None

The target information, or None.

named_constants Mapping[str, VariableInfo]

A copy of named_constants as a dict from token to VariableInfo, in the library's order of "lit" symbols.

Examples:

>>> from SRToolkit.utils import SymbolLibrary
>>> from SRToolkit.utils.expression_constraints import MaxTreeDepth
>>> bk = BackgroundKnowledge(
...     SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(["+", "*", "C"], num_variables=2),
...     description=(
...         "Voltage measured across metal conductors of different resistance, each carrying "
...         "a steady current, at room temperature. Without current there is no voltage; the "
...         "voltage grows with the current and with the resistance."
...     ),
...     variables={"X_0": VariableInfo("I", "current"), "X_1": VariableInfo("R", "resistance")},
...     target=VariableInfo("U", "voltage"),
...     constraints=[MaxTreeDepth(4)])
>>> bk.constant_bounds
(-5.0, 5.0)
>>> bk.variables["X_0"].name
'I'

def sampling_grammar(self) -> Grammar:
    """Return the grammar to sample expressions from.

    ``reference_grammar`` if it is set (logged at ``INFO`` level), otherwise a generic grammar
    for ``symbol_library``
    ([Grammar.from_symbol_library][SRToolkit.utils.grammar.Grammar.from_symbol_library]).

    Returns:
        The grammar.
    """
    if self.reference_grammar is not None:
        logger.info("Sampling from the reference grammar of the background knowledge.")
        return self.reference_grammar
    return Grammar.from_symbol_library(self.symbol_library)

Contains nothing about the answer. Lines, in this order, each left out when its field is empty or None:

  • Task: <description>
  • Target: <target.describe()> (also left out if that is "")
  • Variables: then one line <token>: <VariableInfo.describe()> per entry of variables, in the library's variable order (just <token> if it describes to "")
  • Named constants: then one line <token>: <VariableInfo.describe()> per entry of named_constants, in the library's order of "lit" symbols (just <token> if it describes to "")

  • Enforced constraints (expressions that break them are rejected): then - <constraint> per required constraint
  • Hints (advisory, may be ignored): then - <constraint> per advisory constraint

A constraint is written as its describe, e.g. expression tree at most 4 levels deep. A sampler is written as its describe, e.g. uniform on [1, 5].

...     description="Toy task", variables={"X_0": VariableInfo("x", "position")})

def describe(self, required_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] = ()) -> str:
    r"""Return a plain-text description of the task for people and LLM prompts.

    Contains nothing about the answer. Lines, in this order, each left out when its field is
    empty or ``None``:

    - ``Task: <description>``
    - ``Target: <target.describe()>`` (also left out if that is ``""``)
    - ``Variables:`` then one line ``  <token>: <VariableInfo.describe()>`` per entry of
      ``variables``, in the library's variable order (just ``  <token>`` if it describes to
      ``""``)
    - ``Named constants:`` then one line ``  <token>: <VariableInfo.describe()>`` per entry of
      ``named_constants``, in the library's order of ``"lit"`` symbols (just ``  <token>`` if it
      describes to ``""``)
    - ``Symbols: <str(symbol_library)>`` (always present)
    - only if the library has a ``"const"`` symbol: ``Free constants are fitted in
      [<lower>, <upper>].`` if the default spec equals ``uniform_default(constant_bounds)``
      (compared by ``to_dict``), otherwise ``Free constants without a spec: <prior>, fitted in
      [<lower>, <upper>].``, with ``<prior>`` the default spec's
      ``prior.describe()`` and the bounds those of the default spec, each written with ``str``
      of a ``float`` (e.g. ``[0.0, inf]``)
    - ``Input distribution:`` then ``  <token>: <sampler>`` per variable (only with samplers)
    - ``Enforced constraints (expressions that break them are rejected):`` then
      ``  - <constraint>`` per required constraint
    - ``Hints (advisory, may be ignored):`` then ``  - <constraint>`` per advisory constraint
    - ``Reference grammar: given``

    A constraint is written as its
    [describe][SRToolkit.utils.expression_constraints.ExpressionConstraint.describe], e.g.
    ``expression tree at most 4 levels deep``. A sampler is written as its
    [describe][SRToolkit.dataset.sampling.Sampler.describe], e.g. ``uniform on [1, 5]``.

    Args:
        required_constraints: The dataset's required constraints, listed apart from the
            advisory ones. Empty when called on its own;
            [Dataset.describe][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.describe] passes the
            dataset's.

    Returns:
        The description, lines separated by ``"\n"``, without a trailing newline.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.utils import SymbolLibrary
        >>> bk = BackgroundKnowledge(SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(["+", "*"], num_variables=1, const_symbol=None),
        ...     description="Toy task", variables={"X_0": VariableInfo("x", "position")})
        >>> print(bk.describe())
        Task: Toy task
        Variables:
          X_0: x: position
        Symbols: +, *, X_0
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    if self.description:
        lines.append(f"Task: {self.description}")
    if self.target is not None and self.target.describe():
        lines.append(f"Target: {self.target.describe()}")
    if self.variables:
        lines.append("Variables:")
        for token, info in self.variables.items():
            text = info.describe()
            lines.append(f"  {token}: {text}" if text else f"  {token}")
    if self.named_constants:
        lines.append("Named constants:")
        for token, info in self.named_constants.items():
            text = info.describe()
            lines.append(f"  {token}: {text}" if text else f"  {token}")
    lines.append(f"Symbols: {self.symbol_library}")
    if self.symbol_library.constant_symbol is not None:
        default = cast(Constant, self.default_constant)
        lower, upper = cast(tuple[float, float], default.bounds)
        if default.to_dict() == uniform_default(self.constant_bounds).to_dict():
            lines.append(f"Free constants are fitted in [{lower}, {upper}].")
        else:
            prior = cast(Sampler, default.prior).describe()
            lines.append(f"Free constants without a spec: {prior}, fitted in [{lower}, {upper}].")
    if self.samplers is not None and len(self.samplers) > 0:
        lines.append("Input distribution:")
        samplers = cast(tuple[Sampler, ...], self.samplers)  # normalised to a tuple in __post_init__
        for token, sampler in zip(self.symbol_library.get_symbols_of_type("var"), samplers):
            lines.append(f"  {token}: {sampler.describe()}")
    required = tuple(required_constraints)
    if required:
        lines.append("Enforced constraints (expressions that break them are rejected):")
        lines.extend(f"  - {c.describe()}" for c in required)
    if self.constraints:
        lines.append("Hints (advisory, may be ignored):")
        lines.extend(f"  - {c.describe()}" for c in self.constraints)
    if self.reference_grammar is not None:
        lines.append("Reference grammar: given")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def priors(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the advisory constraints as records, the structured form of the hints.

    One [summary][SRToolkit.utils.expression_constraints.ExpressionConstraint.summary] per
    advisory constraint, in order. Constraints of the same kind are all listed, not merged.

    return [c.summary() for c in self.constraints]

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Return a JSON-safe dictionary of this background knowledge.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with ``"format_version": 1`` and one key per field, named as the field:
        ``symbol_library``, ``reference_grammar`` (or ``None``) and each sampler and constraint
        as their own ``to_dict``; ``samplers`` as a list in the library's variable order (or
        ``None``); ``constant_bounds`` as ``[lower, upper]``; ``default_constant`` as its
        [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.free_constants.Constant.to_dict], only when that differs
        from the ``to_dict`` of
        [uniform_default(constant_bounds)][SRToolkit.utils.free_constants.uniform_default]
        (so the dicts of tasks with the usual default spec have no such key); ``variables`` as
        ``{token: VariableInfo.to_dict()}`` in the library's variable order;
        ``named_constants`` likewise in the library's order of ``"lit"`` symbols (``{}`` if
        empty); ``target`` as its ``to_dict`` (or ``None``); ``description`` as given.
    """
    d = {
        "format_version": 1,
        "symbol_library": self.symbol_library.to_dict(),
        "samplers": (
            [s.to_dict() for s in cast(tuple[Sampler, ...], self.samplers)] if self.samplers is not None else None
        ),
        "constant_bounds": list(self.constant_bounds),
        "constraints": [c.to_dict() for c in self.constraints],
        "reference_grammar": self.reference_grammar.to_dict() if self.reference_grammar is not None else None,
        "description": self.description,
        "variables": {token: info.to_dict() for token, info in self.variables.items()},
        "target": self.target.to_dict() if self.target is not None else None,
        "named_constants": {token: info.to_dict() for token, info in self.named_constants.items()},
    }
    # Written only when set, so the dicts (and fingerprints) of datasets with the usual default
    # are unchanged.
    default = cast(Constant, self.default_constant)
    if default.to_dict() != uniform_default(self.constant_bounds).to_dict():
        d["default_constant"] = default.to_dict()
    return d

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "BackgroundKnowledge":
    """Rebuild background knowledge from the output of ``to_dict``.

    Missing keys other than ``symbol_library`` take their defaults (a missing
    ``format_version`` is read as ``1``, a missing ``default_constant`` as
    ``uniform_default(constant_bounds)``); unknown keys are ignored.

    Args:
        d: A dictionary produced by
            [to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge.BackgroundKnowledge.to_dict].

    Returns:
        Background knowledge whose ``to_dict`` equals ``d`` with missing keys filled in, nested
        ones included (e.g. a variable's ``unit``), except ``default_constant``: it is written
        only as described in ``to_dict``, so a missing one stays missing, one equal to the
        usual default spec is dropped and a partial template comes back completed.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``symbol_library`` is missing.
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is not ``1``, or as for the constructor.
        TypeError: As for the constructor.
        ImportError: If a saved sampler or constraint class cannot be imported.
    """
    fmt = d.get("format_version", 1)
    if fmt != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"[BackgroundKnowledge.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {fmt!r}. Expected 1.")
    library = SymbolLibrary.from_dict(d["symbol_library"])
    samplers = d.get("samplers")
    grammar = d.get("reference_grammar")
    target = d.get("target")
    default = d.get("default_constant")
    return cls(
        symbol_library=library,
        samplers=[Sampler.from_dict(s) for s in samplers] if samplers is not None else None,
        constant_bounds=tuple(d.get("constant_bounds", (-5.0, 5.0))),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        constraints=[ExpressionConstraint.from_dict(c) for c in d.get("constraints") or ()],
        reference_grammar=Grammar.from_dict(grammar) if grammar is not None else None,
        description=d.get("description", ""),
        variables={k: VariableInfo.from_dict(v) for k, v in (d.get("variables") or {}).items()},
        target=VariableInfo.from_dict(target) if target is not None else None,
        named_constants={k: VariableInfo.from_dict(v) for k, v in (d.get("named_constants") or {}).items()},
        default_constant=None if default is None else Constant.from_dict(default),
    )

def describe(self) -> str:
    """Return a one-line description: ``"<name>: <description> [<unit>]"``.

    If only one of ``name`` and ``description`` is non-empty, it is written alone, without
    ``": "``. The unit, written with ``str``, is appended in brackets after a space, or alone if
    both are empty; it is left out if ``None``.

    Returns:
        The description, or ``""`` if all fields are empty.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.utils import units as u
        >>> VariableInfo("v", "velocity", u.m / u.s).describe()
        'v: velocity [m s^-1]'
        >>> VariableInfo("v").describe()
        'v'
    """
    text = ": ".join(part for part in (self.name, self.description) if part)
    if self.unit is None:
        return text
    return f"{text} [{self.unit}]" if text else f"[{self.unit}]"
