def __init__(
    self,
    benchmark_name: str,
    datasets: list[Dataset | tuple[str, Dataset]] | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    version: str = "1.0.0",
    base_dir: str | None = None,
):
    """A named, persistent collection of symbolic regression datasets.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> benchmark = Feynman() # Feynman is a specific instance of Benchmark with additional functionality
        >>> len(benchmark.list_datasets(verbose=False))
        100

    Args:
        benchmark_name: Name of this benchmark.
        datasets: Initial datasets to add. Each element can be an
            [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset] instance (auto-named as
            ``"<benchmark_name>_<index>"``) or a ``(name, Dataset)`` tuple.
        metadata: Optional dictionary of benchmark-level metadata (e.g. citation, description).
        version: Version string for this benchmark. Defaults to ``"1.0.0"``.
        base_dir: Directory where dataset files are stored or will be written.
            Optional — if omitted, the data cache is used exclusively.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any element of ``datasets`` is not an
            [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset] or a valid ``(name, Dataset)`` tuple.
    """
    self.benchmark_name = benchmark_name
    self.base_dir = base_dir
    self.version = version
    self.datasets: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    self.metadata = {} if metadata is None else metadata
    if datasets is not None:
        for i, dataset in enumerate(datasets):
            if isinstance(dataset, Dataset):
                self.add_dataset_instance(benchmark_name + "_" + str(i + 1), dataset)
            elif isinstance(dataset, tuple) and isinstance(dataset[0], str) and isinstance(dataset[1], Dataset):
                self.add_dataset_instance(dataset[0], dataset[1])
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    "[Benchmark] Dataset inside the datasets argument must be either a tuple "
                    "(name, Dataset) or a Dataset instance."
                )

def add_dataset_instance(self, dataset_name: str, dataset: Dataset):
    """Adds an instance of the Dataset class to the benchmark.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> benchmark = Feynman() # Feynman is a specific instance of Benchmark with additional functionality
        >>> dataset = benchmark.create_dataset('I.16.6')
        >>> isinstance(dataset, Dataset)
        True
        >>> bm = Benchmark("BM")
        >>> bm.add_dataset_instance("I.16.6", dataset)

    Args:
         dataset_name: The name of the dataset.
         dataset: An instance of the Dataset class.

    Raises:
        Exception: If the dataset name already exists in the benchmark.
    """
    if dataset_name in self.datasets:
        raise ValueError(f"Dataset {dataset_name} already exists in the benchmark.")
    else:
        self.datasets[dataset_name] = {}
    self.datasets[dataset_name]["sr_dataset"] = dataset
    self.datasets[dataset_name]["num_variables"] = dataset.X.shape[1]

def add_dataset(
    self,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    dataset: np.ndarray | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None,
    dataset_name: str | None = None,
    ranking_function: str = "rmse",
    max_evaluations: int = -1,
    ground_truth: list[str] | Expression | None = None,
    original_equation: str | None = None,
    success_threshold: float | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    dataset_metadata: dict | None = None,
    samplers: list[Sampler] | Mapping[str, Sampler] | None = None,
    data_source: DataSource | None = None,
    variables: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] | None = None,
    target: VariableInfo | None = None,
    named_constants: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] | None = None,
    description: str | None = None,
    constant_bounds: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    default_constant: Constant | None = None,
    reference_grammar: Grammar | None = None,
    max_constants: int | None = None,
    max_expr_length: int | None = None,
    required_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] | None = None,
    advisory_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] | None = None,
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    ranking_resample: bool = False,
):
    """Add a dataset to the benchmark without building it.

    The entry is stored in format 5 (see
    [Dataset.to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.to_dict]) and built by
    [create_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.create_dataset]. The
    arguments are validated as by ``Dataset`` before any cache file is written. Array data
    given in ``dataset`` is written to the data cache. A ``UserWarning`` is issued when
    ``ground_truth`` is ``None``.

    Args:
        symbol_library: The symbol library to use.
        dataset: Direct data for the dataset: a bare 2-D ndarray ``X`` (features only; for
            ``"rmse"``, ``y`` is computed from ``ground_truth``), or an ``(X, y)`` tuple. Use ``None`` together with ``data_source`` to have the
            cache layer materialise the data instead. When ``data_source`` is provided
            this argument is ignored. To use data from a local file, load it
            yourself (e.g. with ``numpy.load``) and pass the arrays here.
        dataset_name: The name of the dataset. Auto-generated if ``None``.
        ranking_function: ``"rmse"`` or ``"bed"``.
        max_evaluations: Maximum expressions to evaluate. Negative (default ``-1``) means no limit;
            ``0`` is rejected.
        ground_truth: Ground truth expression, as a token list or an
            [Expression][SRToolkit.utils.expression.Expression] carrying the specs of its
            labelled constants, as for ``Dataset``; read in ``symbol_library``. Saved as
            tokens, its specs as ``ground_truth_constants``.
        original_equation: Human-readable answer, as for
            [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset]; ``None`` is stored as ``None``
            and derived when the dataset is built (see
            [Dataset.original_equation][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.original_equation]).
        success_threshold: Error threshold for success. ``None`` means no threshold.
        seed: Random seed.
        dataset_metadata: Optional dataset-level metadata dict, merged over the benchmark's
            metadata.
        samplers: One sampler per variable, as a list in the library's variable order or a
            mapping ``{token: sampler}``, as for ``Dataset``. They define the problem's
            input distribution and power
            [resample][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.resample]; a
            [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource] draws from them, and a
            ``"bed"`` ranking draws its evaluation points from them.
        data_source: Optional [DataSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.DataSource]
            describing where the data comes from
            ([UrlSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.UrlSource] or
            [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource]). When provided,
            the ``dataset`` argument is ignored and the cache layer manages
            materialisation.
        variables: Information per variable, keyed by token, as for
            [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset].
        target: Information about the target, as for ``Dataset``.
        named_constants: Information per named constant, as for ``Dataset``.
        description: Free text about the task, as for ``Dataset``.
        constant_bounds: Range of the default spec, as for ``Dataset``.
        default_constant: The default spec of free constants, as for ``Dataset``.
        reference_grammar: A grammar an approach may start from, as for ``Dataset``.
        max_constants: Free-constant limit, as for ``Dataset`` (``None``: 8).
        max_expr_length: Token limit, as for ``Dataset`` (``None``: no limit).
        required_constraints: Further required constraints, as for ``Dataset``.
        advisory_constraints: Hints about the search space, as for ``Dataset``.
        settings: Settings of the evaluator, ranking and parameter estimation, as for
            ``Dataset``.
        ranking_resample: Resample the ranking's randomness each run, as for ``Dataset``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the dataset name already exists; ``max_evaluations`` is ``0``; the
            background-knowledge, limit or constraint arguments are rejected as by
            [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset]; ``ground_truth`` is an
            ndarray, or missing where the ranking needs it (``"bed"``, or ``"rmse"`` with a
            bare ndarray ``dataset``, not an ``(X, y)`` tuple); ``dataset`` is a tuple that is
            not two numpy arrays; the data has a different number of columns than the symbol library
            has variables; both ``dataset`` and ``data_source`` are ``None`` (the
            dataset could never be loaded); a free spec of ``ground_truth`` has a ``value``
            outside the bounds it takes from ``default_constant``; ``"rmse"`` has to generate ``y`` (a bare ndarray ``dataset``, or a
            ``SampleSource``, also inside a ``FallbackSource``) and a free constant of
            ``ground_truth`` has no fixed value in its specs; or ``ground_truth`` cannot be
            evaluated on a bare ndarray ``dataset`` (raised from the original error).
        TypeError: As for ``Dataset``.
        ExpressionParseError: If ``ground_truth`` does not parse.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from SRToolkit.utils import SymbolLibrary
        >>> bm = Benchmark("BM")
        >>> X = np.random.rand(10, 2)
        >>> bm.add_dataset(SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(2), (X, X[:, 0] + X[:, 1]), dataset_name="test_ds",
        ...     ground_truth=["X_0", "+", "X_1"], original_equation="y = x0 + x1")
        >>> len(bm.list_datasets(verbose=False))
        1
    """
    if dataset_name is None:
        dataset_name = f"{self.benchmark_name}_{len(self.datasets) + 1}"

    # Fail fast before any cache files are written, mirroring add_dataset_instance.
    if dataset_name in self.datasets:
        raise ValueError(f"[Benchmark.add_dataset] Dataset '{dataset_name}' already exists in the benchmark.")
    if max_evaluations == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "[Benchmark.add_dataset] max_evaluations must be positive, or negative for no limit; got 0."
        )

    # Validate the task (background knowledge, required constraints) before anything is written.
    # Array data is checked against the library too (dataset is ignored when data_source is given).
    X = None
    if data_source is None:
        if isinstance(dataset, np.ndarray):
            X = dataset
        elif isinstance(dataset, tuple) and len(dataset) == 2 and isinstance(dataset[0], np.ndarray):
            X = dataset[0]
    bk, required, settings = _resolve_task(
        {
            "symbol_library": symbol_library,
            "samplers": samplers,
            "variables": variables,
            "target": target,
            "named_constants": named_constants,
            "description": description,
            "constant_bounds": constant_bounds,
            "default_constant": default_constant,
            "reference_grammar": reference_grammar,
            "constraints": advisory_constraints,
        },
        max_constants,
        max_expr_length,
        required_constraints,
        settings,
        ranking_resample,
        X,
    )
    try:
        gt = _as_ground_truth(ground_truth, bk.symbol_library, cast(Constant, bk.default_constant))
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
        raise type(e)(f"[Benchmark.add_dataset] {e}") from None
    # RMSE generates y from the ground truth for a bare X or a SampleSource: its free constants
    # need fixed values, checked here before anything is written.
    parameters = None
    # A SampleSource generates y, also as one of a FallbackSource's sources.
    sources = [data_source, *getattr(data_source, "sources", [])]
    generates_y = any(isinstance(s, SampleSource) for s in sources) or (
        data_source is None and isinstance(dataset, np.ndarray)
    )
    if ranking_function == "rmse" and gt is not None and generates_y:
        parameters = _ground_truth_parameters(gt, f"[Benchmark.add_dataset] Dataset '{dataset_name}'")
    symbol_library = bk.symbol_library
    if dataset is None and data_source is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "[Benchmark.add_dataset] Give the data ('dataset') or a 'data_source' to generate it from; "
            "without either the dataset could never be loaded."
        )

    merged_metadata = copy.deepcopy(self.metadata)
    if dataset_metadata:
        merged_metadata.update(dataset_metadata)

    entry: dict[str, Any] = {
        "format_version": 5,
        "dataset_name": dataset_name,
        "benchmark": self.benchmark_name,
        "version": self.version,
        "ranking_function": ranking_function,
        "max_evaluations": max_evaluations,
        "success_threshold": success_threshold,
        "seed": seed,
        "dataset_metadata": merged_metadata,
        "original_equation": original_equation,
        "settings": settings.to_dict(),
        "ranking_resample": ranking_resample,
        "ground_truth": None if gt is None else list(gt.tokens),
        "ground_truth_constants": (
            [c.to_dict() for c in sorted(gt.free_constants, key=lambda c: c.label or "")]
            if gt is not None and gt.free_constants
            else None
        ),
        "background_knowledge": bk.to_dict(),
        "required_constraints": [c.to_dict() for c in required],
        # Samplers and array data are validated to match the library's variables.
        "num_variables": _count_variables(symbol_library),
    }

    if ground_truth is None:
        if ranking_function == "bed":
            raise ValueError("[Benchmark.add_dataset] For 'bed' ranking, the ground truth must be provided.")
        warnings.warn(
            "[Benchmark.add_dataset] 'ground_truth' argument not provided. We recommend providing it "
            "for more transparent evaluation."
        )

    # Resolve the data source / write the arrays.
    if data_source is not None:
        # Lazy: the cache layer materialises X (and y) on first use; nothing written here.
        entry["data_source"] = data_source.to_dict()
    else:
        entry["data_source"] = None
        if isinstance(dataset, np.ndarray):
            if ranking_function == "rmse":
                if gt is None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "[Benchmark.add_dataset] For 'rmse' ranking, if the dataset argument is a numpy "
                        "array, the ground truth must be provided."
                    )
                try:
                    y = compile_expr(gt)(dataset, parameters)
                except Exception as e:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"[Benchmark.add_dataset] Could not evaluate the ground truth. Original error: {e}"
                    ) from e
                _save_arrays_to_cache(self.benchmark_name, self.version, dataset_name, dataset, y)
            elif ranking_function == "bed":
                _save_arrays_to_cache(self.benchmark_name, self.version, dataset_name, dataset)

        elif isinstance(dataset, tuple):
            if (
                len(dataset) != 2
                or not isinstance(dataset[0], np.ndarray)
                or not isinstance(dataset[1], np.ndarray)
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    "[Benchmark.add_dataset] When the dataset argument is a tuple, it must be (X, y) "
                    "with both values numpy arrays."
                )
            if ranking_function == "bed":
                warnings.warn(
                    "[Benchmark.add_dataset] 'bed' ranking only utilizes the array with features. "
                    "Array with targets will be ignored."
                )
            _save_arrays_to_cache(self.benchmark_name, self.version, dataset_name, dataset[0], dataset[1])

    self.datasets[dataset_name] = entry

def add_from_samplers(
    self,
    ground_truth: list[str] | Expression,
    samplers: list[Sampler] | Mapping[str, Sampler] | None = None,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary | None = None,
    n_samples: int = 10000,
    seed: int | None = None,
    ranking_function: str = "rmse",
    dataset_name: str | None = None,
    original_equation: str | None = None,
    success_threshold: float | None = None,
    max_evaluations: int = -1,
    dataset_metadata: dict | None = None,
    variables: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] | None = None,
    target: VariableInfo | None = None,
    named_constants: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] | None = None,
    description: str | None = None,
    constant_bounds: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    default_constant: Constant | None = None,
    reference_grammar: Grammar | None = None,
    max_constants: int | None = None,
    max_expr_length: int | None = None,
    required_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] | None = None,
    advisory_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] | None = None,
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    ranking_resample: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Add a dataset described by a ground-truth expression and per-variable samplers.

    The benchmark-level counterpart to
    [Dataset.from_samplers][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.from_samplers]: it
    attaches a [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource], so the data is
    generated lazily from the samplers (and, for RMSE, ``ground_truth``) the first time the
    dataset is materialised via
    [create_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.create_dataset]. Nothing is
    written to the data cache here.

    Args:
        ground_truth: Ground-truth expression as a token list or an
            [Expression][SRToolkit.utils.expression.Expression] with its specs; with
            ``ranking_function="rmse"``, every free constant in it needs a fixed value in its
            specs.
        samplers: One [Sampler][SRToolkit.dataset.sampling.Sampler] per variable, as a list
            in the library's variable order or a mapping ``{token: sampler}``.
        symbol_library: Token vocabulary. ``None`` uses the library of an ``Expression`` ground
            truth, and for a token list
            [default_symbols][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.default_symbols]
            with one variable per sampler.
        n_samples: Number of input rows to generate on materialisation. Defaults to ``10000``.
        seed: Random seed stored on the
            [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource].
        ranking_function: ``"rmse"`` or ``"bed"``.
        dataset_name: Name of the dataset. Auto-generated if ``None``.
        original_equation: As for
            [add_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.add_dataset].
        success_threshold: Error threshold for success. ``None`` means no threshold.
        max_evaluations: Maximum expressions to evaluate. Negative (default ``-1``) means no limit;
            ``0`` is rejected.
        dataset_metadata: Optional dataset-level metadata dict.
        variables: Information per variable, as for
            [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset].
        target: Information about the target, as for ``Dataset``.
        named_constants: Information per named constant, as for ``Dataset``.
        description: Free text about the task, as for ``Dataset``.
        constant_bounds: Range of the default spec, as for ``Dataset``.
        default_constant: The default spec of free constants, as for ``Dataset``.
        reference_grammar: A grammar an approach may start from, as for ``Dataset``.
        max_constants: Free-constant limit, as for ``Dataset`` (``None``: 8).
        max_expr_length: Token limit, as for ``Dataset`` (``None``: no limit).
        required_constraints: Further required constraints, as for ``Dataset``.
        advisory_constraints: Hints about the search space, as for ``Dataset``.
        settings: Settings of the evaluator, ranking and parameter estimation, as for
            ``Dataset``.
        ranking_resample: Resample the ranking's randomness each run, as for ``Dataset``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``samplers`` is ``None`` or empty, or as for
            [add_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.add_dataset].
        TypeError: As for ``add_dataset``.
        ExpressionParseError: As for ``add_dataset``.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset.sampling import UniformSampling
        >>> bm = Benchmark("BM")
        >>> bm.add_from_samplers(["X_0", "+", "X_1"],
        ...     [UniformSampling(0, 5), UniformSampling(0, 5)], dataset_name="add",
        ...     n_samples=100, seed=0)
        >>> ds = bm.create_dataset("add")
        >>> ds.X.shape
        (100, 2)
    """
    if not samplers:
        raise ValueError(
            "[Benchmark.add_from_samplers] 'samplers' must be non-empty (one sampler per input variable)."
        )
    if symbol_library is None:
        symbol_library = (
            ground_truth.symbol_library
            if isinstance(ground_truth, Expression)
            else SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(len(samplers))
        )

    self.add_dataset(
        symbol_library=symbol_library,
        dataset=None,
        dataset_name=dataset_name,
        ranking_function=ranking_function,
        max_evaluations=max_evaluations,
        ground_truth=ground_truth,
        original_equation=original_equation,
        success_threshold=success_threshold,
        seed=seed,
        dataset_metadata=dataset_metadata,
        samplers=samplers,
        data_source=SampleSource(n_samples=n_samples, seed=seed),
        variables=variables,
        target=target,
        named_constants=named_constants,
        description=description,
        constant_bounds=constant_bounds,
        default_constant=default_constant,
        reference_grammar=reference_grammar,
        max_constants=max_constants,
        max_expr_length=max_expr_length,
        required_constraints=required_constraints,
        advisory_constraints=advisory_constraints,
        settings=settings,
        ranking_resample=ranking_resample,
    )

def create_dataset(
    self,
    dataset_name: str,
    n_samples: int | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> Dataset:
    """Create the dataset stored under ``dataset_name``.

    When ``n_samples`` is provided the returned dataset contains freshly sampled data
    instead of the pre-generated data on disk. The dataset must have samplers defined
    (see ``samplers`` argument of
    [add_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.add_dataset]). Entries of formats
    2–4 from older saved benchmarks are migrated as by
    [Dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.from_dict].

    Args:
        dataset_name: The name of the dataset to create.
        n_samples: If provided, generate a fresh dataset with this many samples using
            the stored samplers instead of loading pre-generated data from disk.
        seed: Random seed used when ``n_samples`` is provided. If ``None``, no seed is set.

    Returns:
        An [Dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset] instance containing the
        data, ground truth expression, and metadata for the given dataset.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the dataset name is not found; ``n_samples`` is provided but the
            dataset has no samplers defined; or ``Dataset.from_dict`` raises a ``ValueError``
            for the entry (raised from it, with the dataset name).
        TypeError: As for ``Dataset.from_dict``, unchanged.
        ImportError: As for ``Dataset.from_dict``, unchanged.
        FileNotFoundError: As for ``Dataset.from_dict``, unchanged.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> benchmark = Feynman() # Feynman is a specific instance of Benchmark with additional functionality
        >>> dataset = benchmark.create_dataset('I.16.6')
        >>> dataset.X.shape
        (10000, 3)
        >>> dataset_small = benchmark.create_dataset('I.16.6', n_samples=500, seed=0)
        >>> dataset_small.X.shape
        (500, 3)
    """
    if dataset_name not in self.datasets:
        raise ValueError(f"Dataset {dataset_name} not found")

    if n_samples is not None:
        config = self.datasets[dataset_name]
        if _config_samplers(config) is None:
            raise ValueError(f"[Benchmark.create_dataset] Cannot resample '{dataset_name}': no samplers defined.")
        # _create_from_entry may return the benchmark's stored Dataset instance
        # (for entries added via add_dataset_instance). Copy before mutating X/y so
        # resampling never corrupts the stored dataset or aliases across callers.
        dataset = copy.deepcopy(self._create_from_entry(config))
        return dataset.resample_inplace(n_samples, seed=seed)

    # Loading canonical data: materialisation is driven entirely by each dataset's
    # ``data_source`` — the built-ins use a FallbackSource that downloads the canonical
    # archive once and regenerates from samplers only if the download is unavailable.
    return self._create_from_entry(self.datasets[dataset_name])

def list_datasets(self, verbose: bool = True, num_variables: int = -1) -> list[str]:
    """Return the names of the datasets, optionally printing a line per dataset.

    Nothing is built. With ``verbose``, each line gives the name, the number of variables and
    the equation: the entry's ``original_equation``, or derived as for
    [Dataset.original_equation][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.original_equation]
    when not given (for an entry added with ``add_dataset_instance``, that dataset's
    ``original_equation``). An entry without an equation shows only its name and number of
    variables.

    Args:
        verbose: If ``True``, print one line per dataset.
        num_variables: If not ``-1``, only return datasets with this many input variables.

    Returns:
        The dataset names, sorted by number of variables, then by name.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> benchmark = Feynman() # Feynman is a specific instance of Benchmark with additional functionality
        >>> len(benchmark.list_datasets(num_variables=2, verbose=False))
        15
        >>> datasets_with_8_vars = benchmark.list_datasets(num_variables=8, verbose=False)
        >>> datasets_with_8_vars[0]
        'II.36.38'
    """
    datasets = [
        dataset_name
        for dataset_name in self.datasets
        if num_variables < 0 or self.datasets[dataset_name].get("num_variables") == num_variables
    ]
    datasets = sorted(
        datasets,
        key=lambda dataset_name: (
            self.datasets[dataset_name].get("num_variables", -1),
            dataset_name,
        ),
    )

    if verbose:
        part1 = []
        part2 = []
        part3 = []
        max_length_1 = 0
        max_length_2 = 0
        for d in datasets:
            nv = self.datasets[d].get("num_variables", -1)
            if nv == 1:
                variable_str = "1 variable"
            elif nv is None or nv < 1:
                variable_str = "Amount of variables unknown"
            else:
                variable_str = f"{nv} variables"
            part1.append(d + ":")
            part2.append(variable_str)
            entry = self.datasets[d]
            if "sr_dataset" in entry:
                equation = entry["sr_dataset"].original_equation
            elif entry.get("original_equation") is not None or entry.get("ground_truth") is None:
                equation = entry.get("original_equation")
            else:
                bk = entry.get("background_knowledge") or {}
                target = bk.get("target")
                equation = _derive_equation(
                    entry["ground_truth"],
                    {k: VariableInfo.from_dict(v) for k, v in (bk.get("variables") or {}).items()},
                    VariableInfo.from_dict(target) if target is not None else None,
                )
            part3.append(equation)
            if len(d) + 1 > max_length_1:
                max_length_1 = len(d) + 1
            if len(variable_str) > max_length_2:
                max_length_2 = len(variable_str)

        for p1, p2, p3 in zip(part1, part2, part3):
            line = f"{p1:<{max_length_1}} {p2:<{max_length_2}}"
            print(line if p3 is None else f"{line}, Expression: {p3}")
    return datasets

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Serialise the benchmark to a pure JSON-safe dictionary.

    Dataset entries that have an ``sr_dataset`` key (added via
    [add_dataset_instance][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.add_dataset_instance])
    are serialised via ``Dataset.to_dict()``.

    Returns:
        A JSON-safe dict representing the full benchmark configuration.
    """
    datasets_out = {}
    for name, entry in self.datasets.items():
        if "sr_dataset" in entry:
            datasets_out[name] = entry["sr_dataset"].to_dict()
        else:
            datasets_out[name] = {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "sr_dataset"}

    return {
        "format_version": 2,
        "type": "Benchmark",
        "benchmark_name": self.benchmark_name,
        "version": self.version,
        "metadata": self.metadata,
        "datasets": datasets_out,
    }

    [Dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.from_dict]. The entries are
    copied, so ``d`` is not changed.

    Args:
        d: A dict produced by [to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark.to_dict],
            or a path to a JSON file.

    Returns:
        An [Benchmark][SRToolkit.dataset.benchmark.Benchmark] instance.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``d`` is a ``.zip`` path.
    """
    if isinstance(d, (str, Path)):
        if str(d).endswith(".zip"):
            raise ValueError(
                "[Benchmark.from_dict] Received a '.zip' path. Load archives with SRToolkit.share.load(path)."
            )
        with open(d) as f:
            dd = json.load(f)
    else:
        dd = d

    benchmark_name = dd["benchmark_name"]
    version = dd.get("version", "1.0.0")
    metadata = dd.get("metadata", {})

    b = cls(benchmark_name, version=version, metadata=metadata)

    for name, entry in dd.get("datasets", {}).items():
        # Store a copy of the entry (the caller's dict is not changed); materialisation is lazy
        # via create_dataset.
        entry = copy.deepcopy(entry)
        b.datasets[name] = entry
        if "num_variables" not in entry:
            # Try to infer
            samplers = _config_samplers(entry)
            if samplers is not None:
                entry["num_variables"] = len(samplers)
            else:
                entry["num_variables"] = -1

    return b

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, d: dict | None) -> "DataSource" | None:
    """Reconstruct a source from a dict produced by
    [to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.DataSource.to_dict].

    When called on the base [DataSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.DataSource]
    class, dispatches to the concrete subclass named by the ``"source_class"`` key
    using ``importlib`` — both built-in and user-defined subclasses round-trip without
    a central registry. When called on a concrete subclass, that subclass must override
    this method.

    Args:
        d: Dictionary with a ``"source_class"`` key (fully-qualified class path) and the
            source's parameters, or ``None`` (data is already cached / supplied directly).

    Returns:
        A reconstructed [DataSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.DataSource] instance,
        or ``None`` if ``d`` is ``None``.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``"source_class"`` is missing from ``d`` (dispatch path).
        ImportError: If the class cannot be imported (dispatch path).
        TypeError: If the class is not a DataSource subclass (dispatch path).
        NotImplementedError: If called on a subclass that has not overridden this method.
    """
    if cls is DataSource:
        if d is None:
            return None
        d = _auto_bind(d)
        resolved = _import_class(d["source_class"], "data source", DataSource)
        return resolved.from_dict(d)
    raise NotImplementedError(f"{cls.__name__}.from_dict is not implemented.")

FallbackSource(sources: list[DataSource])

Bases: DataSource

A chain of data sources tried in order until one succeeds.

materialize attempts each source's materialize in turn; if one raises, a warning is emitted and the next is tried. The first to succeed wins; if all fail, a RuntimeError chaining the last error is raised.

The built-in benchmarks use this to prefer canonical downloaded data while keeping a network-free fallback — FallbackSource([UrlSource(archive), SampleSource(seed=...)]) downloads the authoritative archive when reachable and regenerates from the dataset's samplers otherwise. Because the whole chain is serialised in the config, the preference travels: a grid recipe, a share.save archive, or a cold worker each download the canonical data first and only sample if it is unavailable — unlike a bare SampleSource, which would always regenerate.

def from_dict(cls, d: dict | None) -> "FallbackSource":
    """Deserialize a [FallbackSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.FallbackSource] from a dictionary produced by its ``to_dict``.

    Args:

        ValueError: If ``d`` is ``None``.

    if d is None:
        raise ValueError("[FallbackSource.from_dict] requires a dictionary, got None.")
    sources = []
    for s in d["sources"]:
        ds = DataSource.from_dict(s)
        if ds is not None:
            sources.append(ds)
    if len(sources) > 0:
        return cls(sources)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[FallbackSource.from_dict] Could not construct at least one DataSource for dictionary: {json.dumps(d)}"
        )

def materialize(self, cache_path: Path, config: dict) -> None:
    """Try each source in order; warn and continue on failure, re-raising if all fail.

    Args:
        cache_path: Target ``.npz`` path inside the data cache.
        config: The dataset's config dict, passed to each source.
    """
    last_exc: Exception | None = None
    for i, source in enumerate(self.sources):
        try:
            source.materialize(cache_path, config)
            return
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - fall through to the next source in the chain
            last_exc = exc
            if i + 1 < len(self.sources):
                warnings.warn(
                    f"[FallbackSource] {type(source).__name__} failed to materialise "
                    f"({exc}); trying the next fallback.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"[FallbackSource] All {len(self.sources)} sources failed to materialise; last error: {last_exc}"
    ) from last_exc

def materialize(self, cache_path: Path, config: dict) -> None:
    """Generate ``X`` (and ``y`` for RMSE) from the dataset's samplers and save them.

    Args:
        cache_path: Target ``.npz`` path inside the data cache.
        config: The dataset's config dict; its samplers, ``ranking_function``,
            ``ground_truth``, ``ground_truth_constants`` and symbol library are used to generate
            the data. The samplers
            and symbol library are read from ``"background_knowledge"`` (format 4) or from
            the top level (formats 2 and 3).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the config has no samplers, or ``ranking_function`` is ``"rmse"`` and
            ``ground_truth`` is missing, an ndarray, or has a free constant without a fixed value
            in ``ground_truth_constants``, or its ``ground_truth_constants`` do not fit it (a
            spec without a label, two specs with one label, or a label that is not a labelled
            constant of it).
    """
    samplers_raw = _config_samplers(config)
    if not samplers_raw:
        raise ValueError(
            "[SampleSource.materialize] Cannot generate data: the dataset defines no "
            "'samplers'. A SampleSource requires samplers (one per input variable)."
        )

    if self.seed is not None:
        np.random.seed(self.seed)

    samplers = [Sampler.from_dict(s) for s in samplers_raw]
    X = _sample_inputs(samplers, self.n_samples)

    ranking_function = config.get("ranking_function", "rmse")
    ground_truth = config.get("ground_truth")
    y = None

    if ranking_function == "rmse":
        if ground_truth is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "[SampleSource.materialize] Cannot generate data: ranking_function is "
                "'rmse' but the dataset has no 'ground_truth'. A SampleSource produces "
                "targets 'y' by evaluating the ground-truth expression on the sampled "
                "inputs, so a ground truth is required. Provide one, or supply X/y "
                "directly (data_source=None)."
            )
        if isinstance(ground_truth, np.ndarray):
            raise ValueError(
                "[SampleSource.materialize] ranking_function is 'rmse' but 'ground_truth' "
                "is a numpy array (a behaviour matrix). Behaviour matrices are a 'bed' "
                "concept and cannot be evaluated to produce targets 'y'. Provide the "
                "ground truth as a token list for RMSE datasets."
            )
        # Format 4 keeps the symbol library in "background_knowledge"; formats 2 and 3 at the top level.
        bk = config.get("background_knowledge")
        sl_dict = bk.get("symbol_library") if isinstance(bk, dict) else config.get("symbol_library")
        if sl_dict is not None:
            sl = SymbolLibrary.from_dict(sl_dict)
        else:
            sl = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(X.shape[1])
        context = f"[SampleSource.materialize] Dataset '{config.get('dataset_name', 'unnamed')}'"
        specs = [Constant.from_dict(c) for c in config.get("ground_truth_constants") or ()]
        try:
            expr = Expression(ground_truth, sl, specs)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"{context} 'ground_truth_constants': {e}") from None
        y = compile_expr(expr)(X, _ground_truth_parameters(expr, context))

    cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if y is not None:
        np.savez(str(cache_path), X=X, y=y)
    else:
        np.savez(str(cache_path), X=X)

def materialize(self, cache_path: Path, config: dict) -> None:
    """Download the archive and extract its data files into the dataset's version directory.

    Args:
        cache_path: Target path, as given by
            [dataset_path][SRToolkit.dataset.data_cache.dataset_path]. The archive is extracted
            into the version folder of its benchmark, also for test and aux keys.
        config: The dataset's config dict (unused).

    Raises:
        urllib.error.URLError: If the archive cannot be downloaded.
        TimeoutError: If the server sends nothing for 60 seconds.
        RuntimeError: If the archive has no file for this dataset's key.
        ValueError: If an archive member would land outside the version folder; nothing is
            written then.
    """
    from SRToolkit.dataset import data_cache

    # <data_root>/<benchmark>/<version_slug>, also for keys with a "/" (test and aux splits).
    benchmark, slug = cache_path.relative_to(data_cache.data_root()).parts[:2]
    version_dir = data_cache.data_root() / benchmark / slug

    # Download to a temporary file rather than into memory; the timeout keeps a dead server from
    # hanging the call.
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as archive:
        with urlopen(self.url, timeout=_URL_TIMEOUT) as response:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, archive)
        archive.seek(0)
        with ZipFile(archive) as zf:
            names = zf.namelist()
            if "manifest.json" in names:  # written by share.save
                prefix = f"data/{benchmark}/{slug}/"
            elif any(name.startswith("data/") for name in names):  # the built-in benchmarks' hosted archives
                prefix = "data/"
            else:
                prefix = ""
            # The archive may come from an untrusted URL: check every destination before writing any.
            targets = {}
            for name in names:
                if not name.startswith(prefix) or name.endswith("/"):
                    continue
                target = version_dir / name[len(prefix) :]
                if not target.resolve().is_relative_to(version_dir.resolve()):
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"[UrlSource.materialize] Refusing to extract {name!r}: it leads outside {str(version_dir)!r}."
                    )
                targets[name] = target
            for name, target in targets.items():
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                target.write_bytes(zf.read(name))
                # Its drift sidecar described the replaced data (resolve writes a new one for cache_path).
                data_cache._meta_path(target).unlink(missing_ok=True)

    if not cache_path.exists():
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"[UrlSource.materialize] After downloading from '{self.url}', the expected "
            f"file '{cache_path}' still does not exist."
        )

def __init__(
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    ranking_function: str = "rmse",
    y: np.ndarray | None = None,
    max_evaluations: int = -1,
    ground_truth: list[str] | Expression | None = None,
    original_equation: str | None = None,
    success_threshold: float | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    dataset_metadata: dict | None = None,
    dataset_name: str = "unnamed",
    samplers: list[Sampler] | Mapping[str, Sampler] | None = None,
    benchmark: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    test_X: np.ndarray | None = None,
    test_y: np.ndarray | None = None,
    aux_data: dict[str, dict[str, np.ndarray] | DataSplit] | None = None,
    variables: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] | None = None,
    target: VariableInfo | None = None,
    named_constants: Mapping[str, VariableInfo] | None = None,
    description: str | None = None,
    constant_bounds: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    default_constant: Constant | None = None,
    reference_grammar: Grammar | None = None,
    max_constants: int | None = None,
    max_expr_length: int | None = None,
    required_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] | None = None,
    advisory_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] | None = None,
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    ranking_resample: bool = False,
) -> None:
    self._background_knowledge, self._required_constraints, self.settings = _resolve_task(
        {
            "symbol_library": symbol_library,
            "samplers": samplers,
            "variables": variables,
            "target": target,
            "named_constants": named_constants,
            "description": description,
            "constant_bounds": constant_bounds,
            "default_constant": default_constant,
            "reference_grammar": reference_grammar,
            "constraints": advisory_constraints,
        },
        max_constants,
        max_expr_length,
        required_constraints,
        settings,
        ranking_resample,
        X,
    )
    self.ranking_resample = ranking_resample

    if max_evaluations == 0:
        raise ValueError("[Dataset] max_evaluations must be positive, or negative for no limit; got 0.")
    self.max_evaluations = max_evaluations
    self.success_threshold = success_threshold
    self.ranking_function = ranking_function
    try:
        self.ground_truth = _as_ground_truth(
            ground_truth, self.symbol_library, cast(Constant, self._background_knowledge.default_constant)
        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
        raise type(e)(f"[Dataset] {e}") from None
    self._original_equation = original_equation

    self.dataset_name = dataset_name

    # The data lives in DataSplits: the train split (X / y, the data the search runs on), an
    # optional held-out test split, and optional extra splits for the user's own measures.
    train_arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"X": X}
    if y is not None:
        train_arrays["y"] = y
    self._train = DataSplit(train_arrays)
    self.test: DataSplit | None = None
    if test_X is not None:
        test_arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"X": test_X}
        if test_y is not None:
            test_arrays["y"] = test_y
        self.test = DataSplit(test_arrays)
    self.aux_data: dict[str, DataSplit] = {}
    for key, value in (aux_data or {}).items():
        self._validate_aux_key(key)
        self.aux_data[key] = value if isinstance(value, DataSplit) else DataSplit(dict(value))

    self.contains_constants = self.symbol_library.constant_symbol is not None

    self.seed = seed
    self.dataset_metadata = dataset_metadata

    # Cache / serialisation metadata
    self.benchmark = benchmark
    self.version = version
    # Origin of the cached data (UrlSource / SampleSource / None). Not a constructor
    # argument: it is set by the factory methods (from_dict, from_samplers) and by
    # Benchmark.add_dataset. End users select an origin through those entry points.
    # data_source is a view over the train split's source (see the property below).
    self.data_source = None

docs.text:
evaluate_approach(approach: Approach, num_experiments: int = 1, top_k: int = 20, initial_seed: int | None = None, results: Results | None = None, callbacks: Callback | CallbackDispatcher | list[Callback] | None = None, verbose: bool = True, adaptation_path: str | None = None, checkpoint_dir: str | PathLike | None = None, resume: bool = False, keep_checkpoint: bool = False, snapshot_interval: float | None = 300.0, keep_all_models: bool = True) -> Results

Run an SR approach on this dataset and collect the results.

Each experiment searches with a new evaluator from create_evaluator. Experiment i (from 0) is seeded with seed + i, where seed is initial_seed or the dataset seed; it is unseeded if both are None. Approaches with adaptation_scope="once" adapt before the first experiment, those with "experiment" before each one.

With checkpoint_dir, each experiment keeps its models and trace in the checkpoint checkpoint_dir/{dataset_name}/{approach_name}/exp_{seed}.sqlite (the layout of an ExperimentGrid; see Checkpoints), and its search, not its adaptation, runs inside stop_on_signals:

  • when every experiment has finished, their checkpoints are deleted (or, with keep_checkpoint=True, kept and compacted, each into one self-contained file);
  • if an experiment is interrupted (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM), no further experiments run: its results are added with stop reason "interrupted", all checkpoints are kept, and a UserWarning says where;
  • if a search raises, all checkpoints are kept (committed and closed), and the exception propagates.

With resume=True, the call continues where an earlier one stopped: finished experiments are read from their checkpoints as they are (without adapting, running or calling callbacks), the interrupted one continues from its last snapshot (or starts anew, with a UserWarning, if the approach lacks the step interface), and the rest run. A finished run is not extended, and its settings are not checked against this call's. Without checkpoint_dir, nothing is written to disk and no signal handlers are installed.

A result refers to its experiment's checkpoint (its checkpoint) exactly when the file remains as the call returns or raises: kept, interrupted or failed.

Every experiment's results are kept in memory until the call returns; for long runs, use keep_all_models=False, or an ExperimentGrid, which saves each experiment's results to its own file.

None checkpoint_dir str | PathLike | None

None resume bool

Continue the experiments whose checkpoints exist in checkpoint_dir. Default False: an existing checkpoint raises FileExistsError.

False keep_checkpoint bool

Keep the checkpoints of finished experiments, e.g. to inspect all their models later. Default False.

False snapshot_interval float | None

Seconds between snapshots in an experiment with a checkpoint; None: only when the approach's step loop ends. Default 300.0.

300.0 keep_all_models bool

As for get_results, for every experiment, including those read from checkpoints. Default True.

def evaluate_approach(
    self,
    approach: Approach,
    num_experiments: int = 1,
    top_k: int = 20,
    initial_seed: int | None = None,
    results: Results | None = None,
    callbacks: Callback | CallbackDispatcher | list[Callback] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
    adaptation_path: str | None = None,
    checkpoint_dir: str | os.PathLike | None = None,
    resume: bool = False,
    keep_checkpoint: bool = False,
    snapshot_interval: float | None = 300.0,
    keep_all_models: bool = True,
) -> Results:
    """Run an SR approach on this dataset and collect the results.

    Each experiment searches with a new evaluator from
    [create_evaluator][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.create_evaluator]. Experiment ``i``
    (from 0) is seeded with ``seed + i``, where ``seed`` is ``initial_seed`` or the dataset seed; it
    is unseeded if both are ``None``. Approaches with ``adaptation_scope="once"`` adapt before the
    first experiment, those with ``"experiment"`` before each one.

    With ``checkpoint_dir``, each experiment keeps its models and trace in the checkpoint
    ``checkpoint_dir/{dataset_name}/{approach_name}/exp_{seed}.sqlite`` (the layout of an
    [ExperimentGrid][SRToolkit.experiments.ExperimentGrid]; see
    [Checkpoints][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator]), and its search, not its adaptation, runs
    inside [stop_on_signals][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.stop_on_signals]:

    - when every experiment has finished, their checkpoints are deleted (or, with
      ``keep_checkpoint=True``, kept and compacted, each into one self-contained file);
    - if an experiment is interrupted (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM), no further experiments run: its
      results are added with stop reason ``"interrupted"``, all checkpoints are kept, and a
      ``UserWarning`` says where;
    - if a search raises, all checkpoints are kept (committed and closed), and the exception
      propagates.

    With ``resume=True``, the call continues where an earlier one stopped: finished experiments
    are read from their checkpoints as they are (without adapting, running or calling
    callbacks), the interrupted one continues from its last snapshot (or starts anew, with a
    ``UserWarning``, if the approach lacks the
    [step interface][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.supports_steps]), and
    the rest run. A finished run is not extended, and its settings are not checked against this
    call's. Without
    ``checkpoint_dir``, nothing is written to disk and no signal handlers are installed.

    A result refers to its experiment's checkpoint (its
    [checkpoint][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult]) exactly when the file remains as the call
    returns or raises: kept, interrupted or failed.

    Every experiment's results are kept in memory until the call returns; for long runs, use
    ``keep_all_models=False``, or an [ExperimentGrid][SRToolkit.experiments.ExperimentGrid],
    which saves each experiment's results to its own file.

    Args:
        approach: The approach to run.
        num_experiments: Number of independent runs.
        top_k: Number of best expressions kept per run.
        initial_seed: Base seed; ``None`` uses the dataset seed.
        results: [Results][SRToolkit.evaluation.results.Results] to append to in place;
            ``None`` creates a new one.
        callbacks: An [Callback][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.Callback], a list of them, or a
            [CallbackDispatcher][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.CallbackDispatcher].
        verbose: Print a line as each experiment starts.
        adaptation_path: For ``adaptation_scope="once"``: the state file passed to
            [adapt_or_load][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.adapt_or_load]; ``None``
            adapts without saving.
        checkpoint_dir: Directory for the experiments' checkpoints, created if missing;
            ``None`` (default) keeps them in memory.
        resume: Continue the experiments whose checkpoints exist in ``checkpoint_dir``.
            Default ``False``: an existing checkpoint raises ``FileExistsError``.
        keep_checkpoint: Keep the checkpoints of finished experiments, e.g. to inspect all their
            models later. Default ``False``.
        snapshot_interval: Seconds between snapshots in an experiment with a checkpoint;
            ``None``: only when the approach's step loop ends. Default ``300.0``.
        keep_all_models: As for
            [get_results][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.get_results], for every
            experiment, including those read from checkpoints. Default ``True``.

    Returns:
        ``results`` (or a new ``Results``) with one entry per experiment run.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``checkpoint_dir`` is given and the experiments are unseeded (``initial_seed``
            and the dataset seed are ``None``): a checkpoint is named by its seed; if
            ``keep_all_models`` is ``False`` and ``top_k <= 0`` (before anything runs). Also as for
            [Evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator] with ``resume=True``
            when an interrupted experiment continues (e.g. its checkpoint is of a run with other
            settings).
        FileExistsError: If ``resume`` is ``False`` and an experiment's checkpoint exists.
    """
    base_seed = self.seed if initial_seed is None else initial_seed
    if checkpoint_dir is not None and base_seed is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "[Dataset.evaluate_approach] checkpoint_dir needs seeded experiments: pass initial_seed or "
            "give the dataset a seed."
        )

    if not keep_all_models and top_k <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"[Dataset.evaluate_approach] keep_all_models=False needs top_k >= 1, got {top_k}.")
    if results is None:
        results = Results()

    if isinstance(callbacks, Callback):
        dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(callbacks=[callbacks])
        callbacks = dispatcher
    elif isinstance(callbacks, list):
        if len(callbacks) == 0:
            callbacks = None
        else:
            callbacks = CallbackDispatcher(callbacks=callbacks)

    dataset_name = self.dataset_name
    checkpoints: list[str] = []
    referring: list[EvalResult] = []  # results of this call that refer to their checkpoint
    adapted = False
    for experiment in range(num_experiments):
        reference = None
        # Experiment i gets base_seed + i, as job i of an ExperimentGrid does.
        seed = None if base_seed is None else base_seed + experiment
        checkpoint = None
        continued = False
        if checkpoint_dir is not None:
            checkpoint = os.path.join(checkpoint_dir, dataset_name, approach.name, f"exp_{seed}.sqlite")
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(checkpoint), exist_ok=True)
            checkpoints.append(checkpoint)
            if resume and os.path.exists(checkpoint):
                if _run_finished(checkpoint):  # from an earlier call: read it, run nothing
                    if verbose:
                        print(f"Experiment {experiment + 1}/{num_experiments}: read from its checkpoint")
                    results += Results.from_checkpoint(checkpoint, approach.name, top_k, keep_all_models)
                    referring.append(results.results[-1])
                    continue
                if approach.supports_steps:
                    continued = True
                else:
                    warnings.warn(
                        f"[Dataset.evaluate_approach] {approach.name} cannot continue from a snapshot, "
                        f"so experiment {experiment + 1}/{num_experiments} starts afresh and replaces its "
                        f"checkpoint {checkpoint}.",
                        UserWarning,
                    )
                    _remove_checkpoint(checkpoint)
        if verbose:
            print(f"Running experiment {experiment + 1}/{num_experiments}")

        event = ExperimentEvent(
            dataset_name=dataset_name,
            approach_name=approach.name,
            success_threshold=self.success_threshold,
            max_evaluations=self.max_evaluations,
            seed=seed,
        )
        if callbacks is not None:
            callbacks.on_experiment_start(event)

        if approach.adaptation_scope == "once" and not adapted:
            self.adapt_or_load(approach, adaptation_path)
            adapted = True
        elif approach.adaptation_scope == "experiment":
            approach.adapt(self.X, self.background_knowledge, self.required_constraints)

        evaluator = self.create_evaluator(
            seed=seed, checkpoint=checkpoint, resume=continued, snapshot_interval=snapshot_interval
        )
        try:
            evaluator._experiment_id = f"{dataset_name}_{approach.name}_{seed}"
            evaluator.register_callbacks(callbacks)
            with evaluator.stop_on_signals() if checkpoint is not None else nullcontext():
                approach.run(evaluator, seed)
            results += evaluator.get_results(approach.name, top_k, keep_all_models=keep_all_models)
            if checkpoint is not None:
                reference = _checkpoint_reference(evaluator._store, checkpoint)
        finally:
            evaluator.close()

        result = results.results[-1]
        # A callback sees the reference only if the file is sure to stay; it is added afterwards otherwise,
        # since the file remains until the call ends (and is deleted then, see below).
        if reference is not None and (keep_checkpoint or evaluator.stop_reason == "interrupted"):
            result.checkpoint = reference
        if callbacks is not None:
            callbacks.on_experiment_end(event, result)
        if reference is not None:
            result.checkpoint = reference
            referring.append(result)
        if evaluator.stop_reason == "interrupted":
            warnings.warn(
                f"[Dataset.evaluate_approach] Experiment {experiment + 1}/{num_experiments} was interrupted; "
                f"its checkpoint is kept at {checkpoint}. Call again with resume=True to continue.",
                UserWarning,
            )
            return results

    for checkpoint in checkpoints:
        if keep_checkpoint:
            _compact_checkpoint(checkpoint)
        else:
            _remove_checkpoint(checkpoint)
    if not keep_checkpoint:
        for result in referring:
            result.checkpoint = None
    return results

extend_run(approach: Approach, checkpoint: str | PathLike, *, max_evaluations: int | None = None, success_threshold: float | None = None, callbacks: Callback | CallbackDispatcher | list[Callback] | None = None, top_k: int = 20, keep_all_models: bool = True, snapshot_interval: float | None = 300.0, adaptation_path: str | None = None) -> Results

Continue the run saved in checkpoint with new limits.

Use it to give a finished or interrupted run a larger budget, a lower threshold or other callbacks (e.g. a longer time limit). The run goes back to its last snapshot and continues from there, with its seed (see Extending runs). If the approach's search depends only on its saved state, not on its limits, the result equals a run that had the new limits from the start.

Limits left as None stay as they were; this dataset's own max_evaluations and success_threshold are not used. If nothing changes (the same limits and callbacks), the call is a plain resume: a finished run stays finished and an interrupted one continues. As in evaluate_approach, the approach adapts first, the callbacks get on_experiment_start and on_experiment_end, and Ctrl-C stops the run cleanly.

The checkpoint must come from this dataset: the same settings apart from the limits. The setting evaluator.max_consecutive_skips is not a limit and cannot change, so a run stopped by it stops again at once. The approach is not checked, so pass the run's approach. If an extension is interrupted, call extend_run again with None limits to continue it. When the run ends, the checkpoint is compacted into one file, which the result refers to.

Note

The checkpoint is extended in place, so afterwards it holds the extended run. def extend_run(
    self,
    approach: Approach,
    checkpoint: str | os.PathLike,
    *,
    max_evaluations: int | None = None,
    success_threshold: float | None = None,
    callbacks: Callback | CallbackDispatcher | list[Callback] | None = None,
    top_k: int = 20,
    keep_all_models: bool = True,
    snapshot_interval: float | None = 300.0,
    adaptation_path: str | None = None,
) -> Results:
    """Continue the run saved in ``checkpoint`` with new limits.

    Use it to give a finished or interrupted run a larger budget, a lower threshold or other
    callbacks (e.g. a longer time limit). The run goes back to its last snapshot and continues
    from there, with its seed (see [Extending runs][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator]). If the
    approach's search depends only on its saved state, not on its limits, the result equals a
    run that had the new limits from the start.

    Limits left as ``None`` stay as they were; this dataset's own ``max_evaluations`` and
    ``success_threshold`` are not used. If nothing changes (the same limits and callbacks), the
    call is a plain resume: a finished run stays finished and an interrupted one continues. As
    in [evaluate_approach][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.evaluate_approach], the
    approach adapts first, the callbacks get ``on_experiment_start`` and ``on_experiment_end``,
    and Ctrl-C stops the run cleanly.

    The checkpoint must come from this dataset: the same settings apart from the limits. The
    setting ``evaluator.max_consecutive_skips`` is not a limit and cannot change, so a run stopped by it
    stops again at once. The approach is not checked, so pass the run's approach. If an extension is interrupted, call
    ``extend_run`` again with ``None`` limits to continue it. When the run ends, the checkpoint
    is compacted into one file, which the result refers to.

    Note:
        The checkpoint is extended in place, so afterwards it holds the extended run. The
        results of the original run do not change: keep them (e.g. with
        [save][SRToolkit.evaluation.results.Results.save]), or copy the checkpoint first if
        you need the original file. Their
        [open_checkpoint][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.open_checkpoint] raises once the
        limits change. For an approach that is deterministic from its state, the extended run
        starts with the original run's calls, so the statistics of its first ``n`` calls (e.g.
        [best_error_within][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.best_error_within] ``([n])``) are
        those of the original run, with ``n`` its ``evaluation_calls``.

    Args:
        approach: The approach of the run, which must implement the step interface (see
            [supports_steps][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.supports_steps]).
        checkpoint: The run's checkpoint.
        max_evaluations: The new total budget, at least the calls the run made; negative for
            no limit; ``None`` (default) keeps the last segment's.
        success_threshold: The new threshold (a negative one is never reached); ``None``
            (default) keeps the last segment's.
        callbacks: An [Callback][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.Callback], a list of them,
            or a [CallbackDispatcher][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.CallbackDispatcher];
            ``None`` for none; the run's earlier callbacks are not reused. Give them in the run's
            order, so they get their saved states (e.g. a longer ``TimeLimitCallback`` counts on from the
            time saved with the snapshot).
        top_k: As for [get_results][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.get_results].
        keep_all_models: As for ``get_results``.
        snapshot_interval: As for [Evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator].
            Default ``300.0``.
        adaptation_path: For ``adaptation_scope="once"``: the state file passed to
            [adapt_or_load][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.adapt_or_load].

    Returns:
        New results with the run's [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult]; its
        ``stop_reason`` is ``"interrupted"`` after Ctrl-C or SIGTERM (with a ``UserWarning``).

    Raises:
        TypeError: Before anything is changed: if ``max_evaluations``
            is not an ``int``, numpy integer or ``None``, or ``success_threshold`` is not a real
            number or ``None`` (``bool`` is rejected for both); if a callback's ``to_dict``
            holds a value that cannot be saved (see
            [serialization][SRToolkit.utils.serialization]).
        ValueError: Before anything is changed: if ``max_evaluations`` is ``0``, or
            non-negative and below the calls the run made (an extension does not shorten a
            run); if ``keep_all_models`` is ``False`` and ``top_k <= 0``; if the approach does
            not support snapshots; if the file is not a checkpoint, or is of a run with other
            settings than this dataset's (the message names them).
        FileNotFoundError: If no file exists at ``checkpoint``.

    Examples:
        >>> import tempfile
        >>> from SRToolkit.approaches import ProGED
        >>> dataset = Dataset(np.array([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]]), SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(1),
        ...                      y=np.array([2.0, 4.0, 6.0]), max_evaluations=5, success_threshold=-1, seed=0)
        >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        ...     first = dataset.evaluate_approach(ProGED(), checkpoint_dir=tmpdir, keep_checkpoint=True,
        ...                                       verbose=False)
        ...     extended = dataset.extend_run(ProGED(), first[0].checkpoint["path"], max_evaluations=10)
        >>> extended[0].evaluation_calls, extended[0].extended
        (10, True)
    """
    if isinstance(max_evaluations, bool) or not isinstance(max_evaluations, (int, np.integer, type(None))):
        raise TypeError(
            f"[Dataset.extend_run] max_evaluations must be an int or None, got {type(max_evaluations).__name__}."
        )
    if max_evaluations == 0:
        raise ValueError("[Dataset.extend_run] max_evaluations must be positive, or negative for no limit.")
    if isinstance(success_threshold, bool) or not isinstance(success_threshold, (numbers.Real, type(None))):
        raise TypeError(
            "[Dataset.extend_run] success_threshold must be a real number or None, got "
            f"{type(success_threshold).__name__}."
        )
    if not keep_all_models and top_k <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"[Dataset.extend_run] keep_all_models=False needs top_k >= 1, got {top_k}.")
    if not approach.supports_steps:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[Dataset.extend_run] {approach.name} cannot continue from a snapshot, so its runs cannot be extended."
        )
    if isinstance(callbacks, Callback):
        callbacks = CallbackDispatcher(callbacks=[callbacks])
    elif isinstance(callbacks, list):
        callbacks = CallbackDispatcher(callbacks=callbacks) if callbacks else None
    # Raises TypeError for a config that cannot be saved, before anything is changed.
    configs = _to_json_safe([cb.to_dict() for cb in (callbacks.get_callbacks() if callbacks else [])], "callbacks")
    store = ModelStore(checkpoint, "read")
    try:
        seed = store.get_header("seed")
        last = _from_json_safe(store.get_header("limits"))[-1]
        saved = store.get_header("fingerprint", {})
        calls = len(store.trace)
    finally:
        store.close()
    if max_evaluations is not None and 0 <= max_evaluations < calls:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[Dataset.extend_run] max_evaluations={max_evaluations} is below the {calls} calls the run "
            "made; an extension does not shorten a run."
        )
    # A copy of this dataset with the new limits builds the run's evaluators.
    dataset = copy.copy(self)
    dataset.max_evaluations = last["max_evaluations"] if max_evaluations is None else int(max_evaluations)
    dataset.success_threshold = last["success_threshold"] if success_threshold is None else float(success_threshold)
    probe = dataset.create_evaluator(seed=seed)
    fingerprint = probe._fingerprint()
    probe.close()
    changed = sorted(
        k
        for k in fingerprint.keys() | saved.keys()
        if k not in ("max_evaluations", "success_threshold") and fingerprint.get(k) != saved.get(k)
    )
    if changed:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[Dataset.extend_run] {os.fspath(checkpoint)!r} is of a run with other settings than this "
            f"dataset's: {', '.join(changed)}."
        )

    if approach.adaptation_scope == "once":
        self.adapt_or_load(approach, adaptation_path)
    elif approach.adaptation_scope == "experiment":
        approach.adapt(self.X, self.background_knowledge, self.required_constraints)

    # An extension that changes nothing is a plain resume: no new segment, and a finished run
    # stays finished. A segment without recorded callbacks (it made no call) matches any.
    unchanged = (last["max_evaluations"], last["success_threshold"]) == (
        dataset.max_evaluations,
        probe.success_threshold,
    ) and (last["callbacks"] is None or _to_json_safe(last["callbacks"], "callbacks") == configs)
    if not unchanged:
        # Reopen the run with the new limits: the new fingerprint, a limit segment starting at the
        # snapshot, and no stop reason, so the resume below rewinds it to the snapshot.
        store = ModelStore(checkpoint, "resume")
        try:
            limits = _from_json_safe(store.get_header("limits"))
            limits.append(
                {
                    "calls": 0 if store.snapshot is None else store.snapshot.num_calls,
                    "max_evaluations": dataset.max_evaluations,
                    "success_threshold": probe.success_threshold,
                    "callbacks": None,  # recorded at the first evaluation, as for a new run
                    "previous_stop_reason": store.get_header("stop_reason"),
                }
            )
            store.set_header("fingerprint", fingerprint)
            store.set_header("limits", _to_json_safe(limits, "limits"))
            store.set_header("stop_reason", None)
            store.commit()
        finally:
            store.close()
    evaluator = dataset.create_evaluator(
        seed=seed, checkpoint=checkpoint, resume=True, snapshot_interval=snapshot_interval
    )
    event = ExperimentEvent(
        dataset_name=self.dataset_name,
        approach_name=approach.name,
        success_threshold=evaluator.success_threshold,
        max_evaluations=evaluator.max_evaluations,
        seed=seed,
    )
    try:
        evaluator._experiment_id = f"{self.dataset_name}_{approach.name}_{seed}"
        evaluator.register_callbacks(callbacks)
        if callbacks is not None:
            callbacks.on_experiment_start(event)
        with evaluator.stop_on_signals():
            approach.run(evaluator, seed)
        results = evaluator.get_results(approach.name, top_k, keep_all_models=keep_all_models)
        reference = _checkpoint_reference(evaluator._store, checkpoint)
    finally:
        evaluator.close()
    interrupted = evaluator.stop_reason == "interrupted"
    if not interrupted:
        _compact_checkpoint(checkpoint)
    result = results.results[-1]
    result.checkpoint = reference
    if callbacks is not None:
        callbacks.on_experiment_end(event, result)
    if interrupted:
        warnings.warn(
            f"[Dataset.extend_run] The run was interrupted; its checkpoint is kept at {checkpoint}. Call "
            "extend_run again to continue it.",
            UserWarning,
        )
    return results

def adapt_or_load(self, approach: Approach, path: str | None, force: bool = False) -> None:
    """Adapt ``approach`` to this dataset, or load its saved adapted state.

    If ``path`` names an existing file and ``force`` is off, the state is loaded from it with
    [load_adapted_state][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.load_adapted_state].
    Otherwise the approach runs [adapt][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.adapt] on
    ``X``, ``background_knowledge`` and ``required_constraints`` and, if ``path`` is set, saves
    the state there with
    [save_adapted_state][SRToolkit.approaches.approach.Approach.save_adapted_state],
    creating its parent directories. An existing file is loaded as is; it is not checked against
    this dataset. Does not check ``adaptation_scope``.

    Args:
        approach: The approach to adapt.
        path: File the adapted state is loaded from or saved to; ``None`` adapts without saving.
        force: Adapt and overwrite the file even if it exists.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If ``path`` is set and the approach does not implement
            ``load_adapted_state`` or ``save_adapted_state`` (whichever is needed).
    """
    if path is not None and not force and os.path.exists(path):
        approach.load_adapted_state(path)
        return
    approach.adapt(self.X, self.background_knowledge, self.required_constraints)
    if path is not None:
        dir_name = os.path.dirname(path)
        if dir_name:
            os.makedirs(dir_name, exist_ok=True)
        approach.save_adapted_state(path)

The evaluator gets the parts of the background knowledge (its constraints as advisory constraints), required_constraints as required (and adds no limits of its own), and ground_truth with its specs. Its background_knowledge is rebuilt from these parts, so its to_dict(), describe() and priors() equal this dataset's.

  • otherwise the dataset seed (0 if None), so every run is scored by the same objective: the same BED points and behaviours, and the same starting point for each expression's fit.

To score held-out data as the search did, pass the returned evaluator's settings and background_knowledge to HoldoutMetric.

def create_evaluator(
    self,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    checkpoint: str | os.PathLike | None = None,
    resume: bool = False,
    snapshot_interval: float | None = 300.0,
) -> Evaluator:
    """Create an [Evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator] for this dataset.

    The evaluator gets the parts of the background knowledge (its ``constraints`` as advisory
    constraints), ``required_constraints`` as required (and adds no limits of its own), and
    ``ground_truth`` with its specs. Its ``background_knowledge`` is rebuilt from these parts, so its
    ``to_dict()``, ``describe()`` and ``priors()`` equal this dataset's.

    It gets ``settings`` with ``evaluator.max_constants`` and ``evaluator.max_expr_length`` set
    to ``-1`` (the limits are in ``required_constraints``) and ``evaluator.ranking_seed``:

    - the one in ``settings``, if set;
    - otherwise unset if ``ranking_resample``, so the ranking uses the evaluator's seed;
    - otherwise the dataset seed (``0`` if ``None``), so every run is scored by the same
      objective: the same BED points and behaviours, and the same starting point for each
      expression's fit.

    To score held-out data as the search did, pass the returned evaluator's ``settings`` and
    ``background_knowledge`` to
    [HoldoutMetric][SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation.HoldoutMetric].

    Args:
        metadata: Metadata to attach to the evaluator; ``dataset_name`` and ``dataset_metadata`` are
            added to it in place.
        seed: Seed of the evaluator; ``None`` uses the dataset seed.
        checkpoint: The evaluator's checkpoint file; ``None`` (default) keeps its models in
            memory.
        resume: Continue the run saved in ``checkpoint``. Default ``False``.
        snapshot_interval: Seconds between the evaluator's snapshots; ``None``: only when the
            approach's step loop ends. Default ``300.0``.

    Returns:
        The configured evaluator.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the ranking rejects the dataset (e.g. RMSE with neither ``y`` nor
            ``ground_truth``), ``snapshot_interval`` is not positive, or as for
            [Evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator] with ``resume=True``.
        ImportError: If an import-path ``ranking_function`` cannot be imported.
        FileExistsError: As for ``Evaluator`` with a ``checkpoint``.
        FileNotFoundError: As for ``Evaluator`` with ``resume=True``.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]])
        >>> dataset = Dataset(X, SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(2), y=np.array([3, 7, 11]))
        >>> float(dataset.create_evaluator().evaluate_expr(["X_1", "+", "X_0"]).error)  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
        0.0...
    """
    if metadata is None:
        metadata = dict()
    if self.dataset_metadata is not None:
        metadata["dataset_metadata"] = self.dataset_metadata
    metadata["dataset_name"] = self.dataset_name

    # The limits are already in required_constraints; -1 adds none of the evaluator's own.
    evaluator = {"max_constants": -1, "max_expr_length": -1}
    # Fix the ranking's randomness per dataset, unless it is resampled each run.
    if not self.ranking_resample and self.settings.evaluator.ranking_seed is None:
        evaluator["ranking_seed"] = self.seed if self.seed is not None else 0
    bk = self.background_knowledge
    return Evaluator(
        X=self.X,
        y=self.y,
        max_evaluations=self.max_evaluations,
        success_threshold=self.success_threshold,
        ranking_function=self.ranking_function,
        ground_truth=self.ground_truth,
        symbol_library=self.symbol_library,
        seed=self.seed if seed is None else seed,
        metadata=metadata,
        required_constraints=self.required_constraints,
        advisory_constraints=tuple(self.background_knowledge.constraints),
        variables=self.background_knowledge.variables,
        target=self.background_knowledge.target,
        named_constants=self.background_knowledge.named_constants,
        description=self.background_knowledge.description,
        reference_grammar=self.background_knowledge.reference_grammar,
        constant_bounds=bk.constant_bounds,
        default_constant=bk.default_constant,
        samplers=None if self.samplers is None else list(self.samplers),
        settings=self.settings.replace(evaluator=evaluator),
        checkpoint=checkpoint,
        resume=resume,
        snapshot_interval=snapshot_interval,
    )

def priors(self) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Return the constraints as records, the structured form of ``describe``.

    An evaluator from ``create_evaluator`` gives the same with
    [Evaluator.priors][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator.Evaluator.priors].
