docs.title: SRToolkit.utils.serialization
docs.text:
Which values can be saved in SRToolkit results and configs, and how they are stored as JSON.

SRToolkit saves results and configurations as JSON (ModelResult, EvalResult, ApproachConfig, HoldoutMetric). Everything you put into augmentation data, ranking data or an approach config must be one of the values in the table below, nested as deeply as you like; anything else makes to_dict raise a TypeError that names the value's type and its location (e.g. obj['augmentations'][2]).

Internally, _to_json_safe encodes a value into JSON-compatible Python objects before json.dump, and _from_json_safe decodes it after json.load. The encoded form appears in saved files, so changing it affects existing results.

Encoding.

Value Encoded as None, bool, int, float, str unchanged (nan/inf stay floats) list new list of encoded elements tuple {"__tuple__": [encoded elements]} dict whose keys are all exactly str, none reserved new dict of encoded values, key order kept any other dict {"__dict__": [[encoded key, encoded value], ...]}, in order np.ndarray, dtype kind b/i/u/f/U {"__ndarray__": True, "dtype": str(arr.dtype), "shape": list(arr.shape), "data": arr.tolist()} np.ndarray, object dtype same marker with "dtype": "object" and elements encoded recursively numpy scalar of kind b/i/u/f/U obj.item() (Python bool/int/float/str)
  • Reserved keys are "__ndarray__", "__tuple__" and "__dict__". A str-keyed dict containing one as a key is escaped through "__dict__". The decoder recognises a marker by the presence of a reserved key, regardless of its value, so user data is never mistaken for a marker. Field order inside a marker is not part of the format.
  • Dict keys may be None, bool, int, float (including nan and -0.0), str, numpy scalars of a supported kind, and tuples of supported keys (recursively); numpy scalars inside tuple keys are converted.
  • For a 0-d array, data is a scalar. Any other value raises TypeError: complex, bytes, set, numpy scalars such as np.bytes_, np.complex128 and np.datetime64, arrays of other dtype kinds, floats wider than 64 bits (np.longdouble on most Linux systems; scalars and arrays), masked arrays (np.ma.MaskedArray), arbitrary objects. Self-referencing (cyclic) structures are not supported.
  • nan and inf rely on Python's json writing and reading the non-standard tokens NaN and Infinity; strict JSON parsers reject them.

Round-trip guarantee. For every supported x, y = _from_json_safe(json.loads(json.dumps(_to_json_safe(x)))) equals x: containers equal element-wise with nan matching nan, arrays with equal dtype and shape, and leaves of the same type (type(y) is type(x); True does not come back as 1). Two exceptions:

  • numpy scalars come back as the equal Python scalar (np.float64 becomes exactly float; np.float32(0.1) becomes 0.10000000149011612);
  • subclasses of int, float and str (e.g. IntEnum, StrEnum) come back as the plain base type. bool keeps its type.

Container subclasses are not preserved: OrderedDict and defaultdict come back as dict, list subclasses as list, a namedtuple as a plain tuple, an ndarray subclass as np.ndarray; array memory order is not preserved.

Legacy markers. Files written by older versions contain {"__ndarray__": true, "data": ...} without dtype and shape; these decode to np.array(data) (numpy's default dtype, shape of data).

docs.title: SRToolkit.utils.settings
docs.text:
Settings of an evaluation run: how expressions are evaluated, fitted and ranked.

A Settings object holds named sections, one per component that reads them. Each section is a frozen dataclass, a subclass of SettingsSection, with its defaults and validation; its class attribute name is its key in Settings. The built-in sections are:

Section Class Read by evaluator EvaluatorSettings the evaluator estimation EstimationSettings the parameter estimator minimize MinimizeSettings the parameter estimator's optimizer rmse RMSESettings RMSE ranking bed BEDSettings BED ranking

A section that is not given holds its defaults, so Settings() is the default run. Each component reads its own section and ignores the others, so one Settings can configure several rankings at once. A custom ranking adds its own section under its own name.

Facts about the task (constant bounds, the default spec of free constants, samplers, the ground truth's constants) are not settings; they belong to the dataset and its BackgroundKnowledge.

Only the fields that differ from their defaults are saved (to_dict), and two Settings are equal when their saved forms are.

Examples:

>>> settings = Settings(minimize={"max_iter": 200}, evaluator=EvaluatorSettings(simplify_expr=True))
>>> settings.minimize.max_iter, settings.minimize.method
(200, 'L-BFGS-B')
>>> settings.replace(minimize={"tol": 1e-8}).minimize.max_iter
200
>>> settings.to_dict()["sections"]["minimize"]
{'max_iter': 200}

A custom section:

>>> from dataclasses import dataclass
>>> @dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
... class MyRankingSettings(SettingsSection):
...     name = "my_ranking"
...     alpha: float = 0.5
>>> Settings(my_ranking=MyRankingSettings(alpha=0.3)).get(MyRankingSettings).alpha
0.3

Base class of a settings section.

A subclass is a @dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False) with a default for every field and sets name. It validates its fields in __post_init__, raising TypeError for a value of the wrong type and ValueError for one out of range or not one of the allowed values, with a message naming <name>.<field>. Field values must be saveable (see serialization); a field holding an object with to_dict / from_dict declares that class as field(metadata={"codec": cls}).

Two sections are equal when they have the same class and the same to_dict(), as Settings are. (Without eq=False, the dataclass compares field by field instead.)

Name Type Description name str

Source code in SRToolkit/utils/settings.py 
def changed(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the fields whose values differ from their defaults, as ``{field: value}``.

    Values are compared by their saved form, so a value equal to the default is left out.
    """
    result = {}
    for f in dataclasses.fields(self):  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        value = getattr(self, f.name)
        if f.default is not dataclasses.MISSING:
            default = f.default
        else:
            assert f.default_factory is not dataclasses.MISSING  # every settings field has a default
            default = f.default_factory()
        encoded = json.dumps(self._encode(f, value), sort_keys=True)
        if encoded != json.dumps(self._encode(f, default), sort_keys=True):
            result[f.name] = value
    return result

def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the changed fields (see ``changed``) in their saved, JSON-compatible form.

    A field with a codec is saved through its value's ``to_dict``.
    """
    fields = {f.name: f for f in dataclasses.fields(self)}  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return {k: self._encode(fields[k], v) for k, v in self.changed().items()}

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls: type[_S], data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> _S:
    """Build the section from the output of ``to_dict``.

    Args:
        data: Saved field values by field name; missing fields take their defaults.

    Returns:
        The section.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``data`` names a field the section does not have, or as for the
            section's validation.
        ValueError: As for the section's validation.
    """
    fields = {f.name: f for f in dataclasses.fields(cls)}  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    unknown = sorted(set(data) - set(fields))
    if unknown:
        raise TypeError(f"[Settings] Section {cls.name!r} has no field(s) {unknown}.")
    values = {}
    for k, v in data.items():
        codec = fields[k].metadata.get("codec")
        values[k] = codec.from_dict(v) if codec is not None and v is not None else _from_json_safe(v)
    return cls(**values)

def __init__(
    self,
    evaluator: EvaluatorSettings | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    estimation: EstimationSettings | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    minimize: MinimizeSettings | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    rmse: RMSESettings | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    bed: BEDSettings | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    **custom: SettingsSection,
) -> None:
    given = {
        "evaluator": evaluator,
        "estimation": estimation,
        "minimize": minimize,
        "rmse": rmse,
        "bed": bed,
        **custom,
    }
    sections = {name: _as_section(name, value, None) for name, value in given.items() if value is not None}

    object.__setattr__(self, "_sections", sections)

def get(self, cls: type[_S]) -> _S:
    """Return the section stored under ``cls.name``, or ``cls()`` (its defaults) if there is none.

    Args:
        cls: The section class.

    Returns:
        The stored section, or ``cls()``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the section stored under ``cls.name`` is not a ``cls``.
    """
    section = self._sections.get(cls.name)
    if section is None:
        return cls()
    if not isinstance(section, cls):
        raise TypeError(f"[Settings] Section {cls.name!r} holds a {type(section).__name__}, not a {cls.__name__}.")
    return section

def replace(self, **sections: SettingsSection | Mapping[str, Any]) -> Settings:
    """Return a copy with sections replaced or updated; ``self`` is unchanged.

    Args:
        **sections: Sections by name. An instance replaces the section; a dict of fields
            updates the current one (a custom section only if it is present). ``None`` is not
            accepted; reset a section with an instance of its defaults. Sections not named are
            kept.

    Returns:
        The new settings.

    Raises:
        ValueError: As for the constructor (a dict for a custom section that is not present).
        TypeError: As for the constructor, or if a value is ``None``.
    """
    new = dict(self._sections)
    for name, value in sections.items():
        new[name] = _as_section(name, value, new.get(name))
    result = Settings.__new__(Settings)
    object.__setattr__(result, "_sections", new)
    return result

def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the settings as a JSON-compatible dict (arrays as serialization markers).

    Returns:
        ``{"format_version": 1, "sections": {name: fields}}`` with the changed fields of each
        section (see [changed][SRToolkit.utils.settings.SettingsSection.changed]); sections
        without changes are left out. The fields of a custom section also hold
        ``"section_class"``, its import path (``module.QualName``).
    """
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for name, section in self._sections.items():
        fields = section.to_dict()
        if not fields:
            continue
        if name not in _BUILT_IN:
            fields = {"section_class": f"{type(section).__module__}.{type(section).__qualname__}", **fields}
        out[name] = fields
    return {"format_version": 1, "sections": out}

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Settings:
    """Rebuild settings from the output of ``to_dict``.

    A dict with a top-level ``_bundle`` key is first bound with
    [bind_config][SRToolkit.bundle.bind_config], so custom section classes resolve to an
    installed ``.srtk`` bundle.

    Args:
        data: The output of [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.settings.Settings.to_dict].

    Returns:
        The settings.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is not ``1`` or a section without
            ``"section_class"`` is not built in; as for the constructor.
        ImportError: If a ``"section_class"`` cannot be imported.
        TypeError: If ``"sections"`` is not a dict of dicts, or a ``"section_class"`` is not a
            subclass of ``SettingsSection`` or is ``SettingsSection`` itself; as for the
            constructor.
    """
    data = _auto_bind(dict(data))
    if data.get("format_version") != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"[Settings] Unsupported format_version: {data.get('format_version')!r}. Expected 1.")
    sections: dict[str, Any] = {}
    sections_data = data.get("sections", {})
    if not isinstance(sections_data, Mapping) or not all(isinstance(e, Mapping) for e in sections_data.values()):
        raise TypeError("[Settings] 'sections' must be a dict of dicts, one per section.")
    for name, entry in sections_data.items():
        entry = dict(entry)
        path = entry.pop("section_class", None)
        if path is not None:
            section_cls = _import_class(path, "settings section", SettingsSection)
        elif name in _BUILT_IN:
            section_cls = _BUILT_IN[name]
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"[Settings] Unknown section {name!r} without a section_class.")
        sections[name] = section_cls.from_dict(entry)
    return cls(**sections)

docs.title: SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library
docs.text:
The token vocabulary of symbolic expressions.

A SymbolLibrary maps each token to a Symbol holding its properties: type, precedence, NumPy and LaTeX templates, Cython dispatch ID and UnitRule. SymbolLibrary.default_symbols lists the predefined tokens.

Symbol types.

  • "op": binary operator (e.g. +, *).
  • "fn": unary function (e.g. sin, sqrt), prefix or postfix (^2).
  • "lit": named constant, a symbol with a fixed value (e.g. pi, e). Elsewhere in the toolkit "named constant" always means a "lit" symbol.
  • "const": the free constant, whose value is fitted during parameter estimation.
  • "var": input variable, a column of the data array X.

Free, labelled and named constants. A library has at most one free constant, a "const" symbol s (C by default). Each occurrence of s in an expression is a separate parameter. The library also knows the labelled constants <s>_<n>, n one or more digits (C_0, C_17): all occurrences of one labelled constant are one parameter. The label is the whole token, so C_1 and C_01 are different parameters. Labelled constants are not entries of symbols; get returns the symbol of s for them. Free constants, bare or labelled, are parameters of an expression; a known value that belongs to the task and has a name of its own (e.g. g) is a named constant ("lit") instead.

Active library. Functions that take an optional library use the active one: the innermost with library: block, else the default set by set_default (see get_active and get_or_default).

Symbol(token: str, type: str, precedence: int, python_str: str, latex_str: str = '', cython_id: int = -1, unit_rule: UnitRule | None = None)

Immutable record of one token of a SymbolLibrary.

Usually built by SymbolLibrary.add_symbol and returned by SymbolLibrary.get.

Attributes:

Name Type Description token str

The token string.

type str

"op", "fn", "lit", "const" or "var" (see the module docstring).

precedence int

For "op", the binding strength, >= 0: OP_ADDITIVE (100), OP_MULTIPLICATIVE (200), OP_POWER (300) or a custom value. For "fn", a positive value (FN_PREFIX, 1000) makes a prefix function and zero or a negative value (FN_POSTFIX, -1000) a postfix one. LEAF (1000) for the other types.

python_str str

Python expression template used in compiled callables, e.g. "np.sin({})". {} (or {0}, {1}) placeholders take the arguments as source text, so a repeated or embedded argument should be bracketed. It may use NumPy as np and the library's modules.

latex_str str

LaTeX str.format template (literal braces doubled) with {} placeholders for the arguments. "" generates a default, shown here rendered: a \text{tok} b for an "op", \text{tok} a for a "fn", tok_{n} for the "const" (n the constant's number; {tok}_{n} if tok contains _), and \text{tok} otherwise.

cython_id int

Dispatch ID of the Cython evaluator; -1 means no C implementation (evaluated through a Python callable).

unit_rule UnitRule | None

How an "op" or "fn" combines the physical units of its arguments (see UnitRule). None gives the rule of the predefined symbol with the same token and type (see default_symbols), otherwise UnitRule.DIMENSIONLESS. Always None for the other types.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If type is invalid, an "op" has a negative precedence, or unit_rule is given for a type other than "op" and "fn" or does not accept the symbol's number of arguments (2 for "op", 1 for "fn").

TypeError

If unit_rule is not a UnitRule or None.

Examples:

>>> s = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(1).get("sqrt")
>>> s.type, s.precedence, s.python_str, s.cython_id
('fn', 1000, 'np.sqrt({})', 14)
>>> s.unit_rule
UnitRule.power(Fraction(1, 2))

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Serialize the symbol to a JSON-safe dictionary.

    Returns:
        The keys ``symbol`` (the token), ``type``, ``precedence``, ``np_fn`` (``python_str``), ``latex_str``,
        ``cython_id`` and, for ``"op"`` and ``"fn"``, ``unit_rule`` as
        [UnitRule.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.units.UnitRule.to_dict].
    """
    d: dict[str, Any] = {
        "symbol": self.token,
        "type": self.type,
        "precedence": self.precedence,
        "np_fn": self.python_str,
        "latex_str": self.latex_str,
        "cython_id": self.cython_id,
    }
    if self.unit_rule is not None:
        d["unit_rule"] = self.unit_rule.to_dict()
    return d

        d: Dictionary with the keys of [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol.to_dict].
            ``cython_id`` may be missing (``-1``) and ``unit_rule`` missing or ``None`` (the
            default rule).

    Returns:
        The reconstructed symbol.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If any other key is missing.
        ValueError: If the symbol is invalid (see [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol])
            or so is the saved unit rule (see
            [UnitRule.from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.units.UnitRule.from_dict]).
    """
    rule = d.get("unit_rule")
    return Symbol(
        d["symbol"],
        d["type"],
        d["precedence"],
        d["np_fn"],
        d["latex_str"],
        d.get("cython_id", -1),
        None if rule is None else UnitRule.from_dict(rule),
    )

Registry of the tokens of symbolic expressions and their properties.

The toolkit uses it to parse, compile, display and generate expressions. Symbols can be selected from the predefined set (see default_symbols) and added with add_symbol. A library can be used as a context manager to make it the active library (see the module docstring).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default symbols list[str] | None

Predefined tokens to include. None adds none besides the variables and the free constant.

None num_variables int

Number of variables, X_0 through X_{num_variables-1}, reading the columns of X in order.

0 modules dict[str, str] | None

Modules that python_str templates of custom symbols may use, as alias → module path (e.g. {"sp": "scipy.special"}). They are imported here. NumPy is always available as np, an alias that is reserved.

None const_symbol str | None

Token of the free constant; None for a library without one.

'C'

Attributes:

Name Type Description symbols dict[str, Symbol]

Mapping from token to its Symbol, in insertion order. Change it only through add_symbol and remove_symbol.

modules

Mapping from alias to module path (a copy of the argument; {} for None).

num_variables

Column of X given to the next "var" added without python_str. Raised by one on every "var" added, never lowered.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If symbols contains a token that is not predefined, or modules uses the alias "np".

ImportError

If a module in modules cannot be imported.

Examples:

>>> library = SymbolLibrary(["+", "*", "sin"], num_variables=2)
>>> library.symbols.keys()
dict_keys(['+', '*', 'sin', 'C', 'X_0', 'X_1'])
>>> library = SymbolLibrary(["+"], 1, modules={"sp": "scipy.special"})
>>> library.add_symbol("gamma", "fn", FN_PREFIX, "sp.gamma({})", r"\Gamma({})")
>>> with SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(num_variables=2):
...     SymbolLibrary.get_active().get("X_1").python_str
'X[:, 1]'
Source code in SRToolkit/utils/symbol_library.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    symbols: list[str] | None = None,
    num_variables: int = 0,
    modules: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    const_symbol: str | None = "C",
) -> None:
    self.modules = dict(modules or {})
    if "np" in self.modules:
        raise ValueError("The alias 'np' is reserved for NumPy and cannot be used in modules.")
    self.module_namespace()

    self._constant_symbol: str | None = None
    if symbols is None and num_variables == 0:
        self.symbols: dict[str, Symbol] = dict()
        self.num_variables = 0
        if const_symbol is not None:
            self._add_constant(const_symbol)
    else:
        selected = SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(symbols or [], num_variables, const_symbol)
        self.symbols = selected.symbols
        self._constant_symbol = selected._constant_symbol
        self.num_variables = num_variables

The arguments are the fields of Symbol, which documents them. Predefined symbols (see default_symbols) are faster than custom ones: they have C implementations for the Cython evaluator, while custom symbols are evaluated through Python callables.

required symbol_type str

required precedence int

Precedence (see Symbol).

required python_str str

Python expression template (see Symbol). For a "var", None or "" gives "X[:, i]" with i the library's num_variables.

required latex_str str | None

LaTeX template; None or "" generates the default for the type.

None cython_id int

Dispatch ID of the Cython evaluator; -1 evaluates through a Python callable. To keep a predefined symbol's acceleration, pass SymbolLibrary.default_symbols()[token].cython_id.

Unit rule of an "op" or "fn", e.g. UnitRule.power(Fraction(1, 3)) for a cube root. None gives the predefined rule for the token and type, otherwise UnitRule.DIMENSIONLESS, so give a custom symbol that accepts physical units its rule.

Raises:

If the symbol is invalid (see Symbol), or symbol_type is "const" and the library has a free constant with another token, or symbol is the free constant and symbol_type is not "const".

Examples:

>>> library = SymbolLibrary(["+"], num_variables=1)
>>> library.add_symbol("sat", "fn", FN_PREFIX, "({0}) / (1 + ({0}))", r"\frac{{{0}}}{{1 + {0}}}")
>>> from SRToolkit.utils import compile_expr
>>> f = compile_expr(["sat", "(", "X_0", ")"], library)

def add_symbol(
    self,
    symbol: str,
    symbol_type: str,
    precedence: int,
    python_str: str,
    latex_str: str | None = None,
    cython_id: int = -1,
    unit_rule: UnitRule | None = None,
):
    r"""Add a token to the library, replacing any symbol with the same token.

    The arguments are the fields of [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol], which
    documents them. Predefined symbols (see
    [default_symbols][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.default_symbols]) are
    faster than custom ones: they have C implementations for the Cython evaluator, while
    custom symbols are evaluated through Python callables.

    Args:
        symbol: Token to register.
        symbol_type: ``"op"``, ``"fn"``, ``"lit"``, ``"const"`` or ``"var"``.
        precedence: Precedence (see [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol]).
        python_str: Python expression template (see [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol]).
            For a ``"var"``, ``None`` or ``""`` gives ``"X[:, i]"`` with ``i`` the library's
            ``num_variables``.
        latex_str: LaTeX template; ``None`` or ``""`` generates the default for the type.
        cython_id: Dispatch ID of the Cython evaluator; ``-1`` evaluates through a Python
            callable. To keep a predefined symbol's acceleration, pass
            ``SymbolLibrary.default_symbols()[token].cython_id``.
        unit_rule: Unit rule of an ``"op"`` or ``"fn"``, e.g. ``UnitRule.power(Fraction(1, 3))``
            for a cube root. ``None`` gives the predefined rule for the token and type,
            otherwise ``UnitRule.DIMENSIONLESS``, so give a custom symbol that accepts
            physical units its rule.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the symbol is invalid (see [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol]),
            or ``symbol_type`` is ``"const"`` and the library has a free constant with another
            token, or ``symbol`` is the free constant and ``symbol_type`` is not ``"const"``.
        TypeError: If ``unit_rule`` is not a [UnitRule][SRToolkit.utils.units.UnitRule] or
            ``None``.

    Examples:
        >>> library = SymbolLibrary(["+"], num_variables=1)
        >>> library.add_symbol("sat", "fn", FN_PREFIX, "({0}) / (1 + ({0}))", r"\frac{{{0}}}{{1 + {0}}}")
        >>> from SRToolkit.utils import compile_expr
        >>> f = compile_expr(["sat", "(", "X_0", ")"], library)
        >>> f(np.array([[1.0], [3.0]]), None)
        array([0.5 , 0.75])
    """
    if symbol_type == "var" and not python_str:
        python_str = f"X[:, {self.num_variables}]"
    new = Symbol(symbol, symbol_type, precedence, python_str, latex_str or "", cython_id, unit_rule)
    if symbol_type == "const" and self.constant_symbol not in (None, symbol):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot add free constant '{symbol}': the library already has '{self.constant_symbol}', "
            "and a library has at most one. Use labelled constants (C_0, C_1, ...) for shared parameters."
        )
    if symbol_type != "const" and symbol == self.constant_symbol:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot redefine '{symbol}' as '{symbol_type}': it is the library's free constant. Call "
            f"remove_symbol('{symbol}') first, or build the library with const_symbol=None or another name."
        )
    if symbol_type == "var":
        self.num_variables += 1
    self.symbols[symbol] = new
    if symbol_type == "const":
        self._constant_symbol = symbol

def remove_symbol(self, symbol: str):
    """Remove a token from the library.

    Examples:
        >>> library = SymbolLibrary(const_symbol=None)
        >>> library.add_symbol("x", "var", 0, "x")
        >>> len(library.symbols)
        1
        >>> library.remove_symbol("x")
        >>> len(library.symbols)
        0

    Args:
        symbol: Token string to remove.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``symbol`` is not present in the library.
    """
    del self.symbols[symbol]
    if symbol == self._constant_symbol:
        self._constant_symbol = None

def get(self, token: str) -> Symbol | None:
    """Return the [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol] of a token.

    Args:
        token: Token to look up.

    Returns:
        The symbol registered for ``token``; otherwise, for a labelled constant of the free
        constant (see the [module docstring][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library]), the free
        constant's symbol; otherwise ``None`` (brackets, numbers, unknown names). A registered
        token wins, so a ``"lit"`` named ``C_1`` is returned as itself.

    Examples:
        >>> library = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(1)
        >>> library.get("+").precedence
        100
        >>> library.get("C_3").token
        'C'
        >>> print(library.get("("))
        None
    """
    symbol = self.symbols.get(token)
    if symbol is not None or not isinstance(token, str):
        return symbol
    base, _, label = token.rpartition("_")
    symbol = self.symbols.get(base)
    if symbol is not None and symbol.type == "const" and label.isascii() and label.isdigit():
        return symbol
    return None

def module_namespace(self) -> dict[str, Any]:

    return {"np": np, **{alias: importlib.import_module(path) for alias, path in self.modules.items()}}

@staticmethod
def from_symbol_list(
    symbols: list[str], num_variables: int = 25, const_symbol: str | None = "C"
) -> "SymbolLibrary":
    """Create a [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary] containing only the specified subset of default symbols.

    The supported token names are those defined in [default_symbols][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.default_symbols].
    The free constant is always included (listing it is allowed); ``const_symbol=None`` leaves
    it out.

    Examples:
        >>> library = SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(["+", "*"], num_variables=2)
        >>> library.symbols.keys()
        dict_keys(['+', '*', 'C', 'X_0', 'X_1'])
        >>> SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(["+"], num_variables=1, const_symbol=None).symbols.keys()
        dict_keys(['+', 'X_0'])

    Args:
        symbols: Token strings to include.
        num_variables: Number of variable tokens (``X_0`` through ``X_{num_variables-1}``).
            Default is ``25``.
        const_symbol: Name of the free constant, as in
            [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary].

    Returns:
        A [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary] restricted to the requested symbols, the variables
        and the free constant.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``symbols`` contains a name that is not in the default set (``C`` is
            not when ``const_symbol`` names another constant or is ``None``), such as a
            whole expression like ``"x/(a + x)"``. Expressions are built from tokens
            (``/``, ``+``, ``C``, variables), their shape can be restricted with a custom
            [Grammar][SRToolkit.utils.grammar.Grammar], and custom tokens are added with
            [add_symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.add_symbol].
    """
    sl = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(num_variables, const_symbol)
    unknown = [s for s in symbols if s not in sl.symbols]
    if unknown:
        if any(re.fullmatch(r"X_\d+", s) for s in unknown):
            hint = f"Only variables X_0..X_{num_variables - 1} exist; increase num_variables."
        elif "C" in unknown:
            hint = f"The free constant is named by const_symbol (here {const_symbol!r})."
        else:
            hint = (
                "Build expressions such as 'X/(C + X)' from tokens ('/', '+', 'C', variables), "
                "restrict their shape with a custom Grammar, or add custom tokens with add_symbol."
            )
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown symbols {unknown}: only default tokens are accepted "
            f"(see SymbolLibrary.default_symbols). {hint}"
        )

    symbols = symbols + [f"X_{i}" for i in range(num_variables)] + ([const_symbol] if const_symbol else [])

    all_symbols = list(sl.symbols.keys())
    for symbol in all_symbols:
        if symbol not in symbols:
            sl.remove_symbol(symbol)

    return sl

Return a SymbolLibrary with all predefined symbols.

The predefined tokens:

  • Operators ("op"): +, -, *, /, ^.
  • Functions ("fn"): u- (negation), sqrt, sin, cos, exp, tan, arcsin, arccos, arctan, sinh, cosh, tanh, floor, ceil, ln, log (base 10), and the postfix ^-1, ^2, ^3, ^4, ^5.
  • Named constants ("lit"): pi, e.
  • Free constant ("const"): const_symbol.
  • Variables ("var"): X_0 through X_{num_variables-1}, reading the columns of X in order.

Unit rules: +, -, u-, floor, ceil: SAME; *: MULTIPLY; /: DIVIDE; ^: EXPONENT; sqrt: power(1/2); ^-1, ^2 ... ^5: power(-1), power(2) ... power(5); all other functions: DIMENSIONLESS.

Number of variables.

25 const_symbol str | None

@staticmethod
def default_symbols(num_variables: int = 25, const_symbol: str | None = "C") -> "SymbolLibrary":
    """Return a [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary] with all predefined symbols.

    The predefined tokens:

    - **Operators** (``"op"``): ``+``, ``-``, ``*``, ``/``, ``^``.
    - **Functions** (``"fn"``): ``u-`` (negation), ``sqrt``, ``sin``, ``cos``, ``exp``, ``tan``,
      ``arcsin``, ``arccos``, ``arctan``, ``sinh``, ``cosh``, ``tanh``, ``floor``, ``ceil``,
      ``ln``, ``log`` (base 10), and the postfix ``^-1``, ``^2``, ``^3``, ``^4``, ``^5``.
    - **Named constants** (``"lit"``): ``pi``, ``e``.
    - **Free constant** (``"const"``): ``const_symbol``.
    - **Variables** (``"var"``): ``X_0`` through ``X_{num_variables-1}``, reading the columns
      of ``X`` in order.

    [Unit rules][SRToolkit.utils.units.UnitRule]: ``+``, ``-``, ``u-``, ``floor``, ``ceil``:
    ``SAME``; ``*``: ``MULTIPLY``; ``/``: ``DIVIDE``; ``^``: ``EXPONENT``; ``sqrt``:
    ``power(1/2)``; ``^-1``, ``^2`` ... ``^5``: ``power(-1)``, ``power(2)`` ... ``power(5)``;
    all other functions: ``DIMENSIONLESS``.

    Args:
        num_variables: Number of variables.
        const_symbol: Token of the free constant; ``None`` for a library without one.

    Returns:
        A new library with the symbols listed above.

    Examples:
        >>> len(SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(num_variables=2))
        31
    """
    sl = SymbolLibrary(const_symbol=None)
    sl.symbols = {s.token: s for s in _DEFAULT_SYMBOLS}
    if const_symbol is not None:
        sl._add_constant(const_symbol)
    for i in range(num_variables):
        sl.add_symbol(f"X_{i}", "var", LEAF, f"X[:, {i}]", f"X_{{{i}}}")
    return sl

def get_active() -> "SymbolLibrary":
    """Return the currently active [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary].

    Checks, in order: (1) the context manager stack, (2) the module-level default set via

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Serialize the library to a JSON-safe dictionary.

    Returns:
        A dictionary for [from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.from_dict]
        with the keys ``format_version`` (``1``), ``type`` (``"SymbolLibrary"``), ``symbols``
        (token → [Symbol.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol.to_dict], in insertion
        order), ``modules`` and ``num_variables``.

    Examples:
        >>> d = SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(["+"], num_variables=1).to_dict()
        >>> d["symbols"]["+"]["unit_rule"]
        {'kind': 'same'}
    """
    return {
        "format_version": 1,
        "type": "SymbolLibrary",
        "symbols": {token: s.to_dict() for token, s in self.symbols.items()},
        "modules": dict(self.modules),
        "num_variables": self.num_variables,
    }

@staticmethod
def from_dict(d: dict) -> "SymbolLibrary":
    """Reconstruct a [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary] from its dictionary form.

    A missing ``format_version`` means ``1``. A dictionary saved before ``modules`` existed has
    a ``"preamble"`` of import lines instead; it is read only if ``modules`` is missing or
    ``None``, and may contain only ``import numpy as np``, which is dropped (NumPy is always
    available).

    Args:
        d: Dictionary with the keys of
            [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.to_dict].

    Returns:
        The reconstructed library.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``symbols`` or ``num_variables`` is missing.
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is not ``1``, the library has more than one
            ``"const"`` symbol, a symbol is invalid (see
            [Symbol.from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol.from_dict]), ``modules``
            uses the alias ``"np"``, or a ``"preamble"`` line is not ``import numpy as np``.
        ImportError: If a module in ``modules`` cannot be imported.
    """
    if d.get("format_version", 1) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[SymbolLibrary.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {d.get('format_version')!r}. Expected 1."
        )
    modules = d.get("modules")
    if modules is None:
        other = [line for line in d.get("preamble", []) if line.strip() != "import numpy as np"]
        if other:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[SymbolLibrary.from_dict] Cannot convert preamble lines {other} to modules; only "
                "'import numpy as np' is supported (other modules never worked with preamble)."
            )
        modules = {}
    symbols = {token: Symbol.from_dict(entry) for token, entry in d["symbols"].items()}
    consts = [token for token, s in symbols.items() if s.type == "const"]
    if len(consts) > 1:
        raise ValueError(f"[SymbolLibrary.from_dict] At most one free constant is allowed, got {consts}.")
    sl = SymbolLibrary(modules=modules, const_symbol=None)
    sl.symbols = symbols
    sl._constant_symbol = consts[0] if consts else None
    sl.num_variables = d["num_variables"]
    return sl

def __str__(self) -> str:
    r"""Return a comma-separated string of all registered token strings.

def __copy__(self) -> "SymbolLibrary":
    """Return a copy of the library that can be changed independently of the original.

    Returns:
        A new [SymbolLibrary][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary] with its own
        ``symbols`` and ``modules`` (the [Symbol][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.Symbol]
        records are immutable and shared).

    Examples:
        >>> import copy
        >>> library = SymbolLibrary(["+"], num_variables=1)
        >>> new = copy.copy(library)
        >>> new.add_symbol("sin", "fn", FN_PREFIX, "np.sin({})")
        >>> str(library), str(new)
        ('+, C, X_0', '+, C, X_0, sin')
    """
    sl = SymbolLibrary(modules=self.modules, const_symbol=None)
    sl.symbols = dict(self.symbols)
    sl._constant_symbol = self._constant_symbol
    sl.num_variables = self.num_variables
    return sl

docs.title: SRToolkit.utils.types
docs.text:
Shared constants and result dataclasses for SRToolkit.

  • Symbol types (VAR, CONST, FN, OP, LIT) tag the entries of a SymbolLibrary.
  • Precedence levels (OP_ADDITIVE, OP_MULTIPLICATIVE, OP_POWER, FN_PREFIX, FN_POSTFIX, LEAF) order symbols for parsing and printing. Custom operators can use values between the levels.
  • ModelResult (one evaluated expression) and EvalResult (one SR run) hold experiment outcomes. Each model has a Status. Both save to JSON through serialization, so everything stored in them must be a value listed there. CheckResult is the outcome of one check of an ExpressionConstraint; a ModelResult saves the failed advisory ones. The trace-based metrics of EvalResult are explained in evaluator.

Precedence stored for atoms (VAR, CONST, LIT). Atoms never take part in precedence comparisons. The large value prevents spurious parentheses if a high-precedence operator is added.

docs.title: Status module-attribute
docs.text:
Status = Literal['ok', 'invalid', 'rejected', 'undefined', 'error']

Outcome of evaluating one expression, stored as ModelResult.status.

  • "ok": scored, with a finite error.
  • "invalid": not a well-formed expression; the parser raised an ExpressionParseError.
  • "rejected": well-formed, but it fails a check of a required constraint of the evaluator (by default the max_constants / max_expr_length limits), or the ranking function rejected it. A failed pre-check means it was not scored; a failed post-check means it was scored and its fit kept, but its error is still +inf.
  • "undefined": scored, but the ranking function gave a non-finite error, e.g. because the expression is undefined at some inputs (sqrt of a negative number, log(0)) or overflows. For RMSE this describes the fitted model: other constants might have been fine.
  • "error": the ranking function, or a check of a required constraint, raised an exception for a well-formed expression. This is a failure of the evaluation, not of the expression.

Every status except "ok" gets the error +inf.

docs.title: STATUSES module-attribute
docs.text:
STATUSES: tuple[str, ...] = get_args(Status)

The values of Status, in the same order. This is also the key order of status_counts.

docs.title: CheckResult dataclass
docs.text:
CheckResult(passed: bool = True, message: str = '', amount: float = 0.0, implemented: bool = True, constraint: str = '', stage: str = '', error: str | None = None)

The outcome of one check of one ExpressionConstraint.

Immutable (a frozen dataclass), so results can be shared. A constraint's pre_check / post_check returns one; it fills in passed, message and amount and leaves constraint and stage empty. When the Evaluator records a result, it stores a copy with constraint and stage filled in.

Attributes:

Name Type Description passed bool

Whether the expression satisfies the constraint. True also when the check is not implemented.

message str

Why the check failed (e.g. "9 constants, limit 8"); may be empty. For a check that is not implemented, says so. The built-in constraints leave it empty when the check passes.

amount float

How far outside the constraint the expression is, in the constraint's own unit (e.g. 1.0 for one constant too many). The built-in constraints return a float that is greater than 0 exactly when the check fails, and 0.0 when it passes. Not validated, so a custom constraint may return any value.

implemented bool

False if the constraint has no such check. The evaluator then ignores the result, whatever passed says: nothing is recorded and nothing is rejected.

constraint str

The class name (type(constraint).__name__) of the constraint that produced it, filled in by the evaluator; "" otherwise.

stage str

"pre" or "post" for the check that produced it, filled in by the evaluator; "" otherwise.

error str | None

None, unless the check raised an exception or returned something other than a CheckResult (treated as a TypeError). The evaluator then records the check as failed, with error set to "<ExceptionType>: <message>", message to "raised <error>" and amount to inf. Such a result says nothing about the expression; leave it out when counting violations.

Examples:

>>> CheckResult().passed
True
>>> CheckResult(passed=False, message="9 constants, limit 8", amount=1.0).amount
1.0

docs.text:
ModelResult(expr: list[str], error: float, parameters: ndarray | None = None, ranking_data: dict[str, Any] = dict(), augmentations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = dict(), status: Status = 'ok', status_detail: str | None = None, advisory_violations: list[CheckResult] = list(), free_constants: tuple[Constant, ...] | None = None)

One evaluated expression: an entry of EvalResult.all_models.

Two models are equal when their to_dict are equal.

Attributes:

Name Type Description expr list[str]

Token list representing the expression, e.g. ["C", "*", "X_0"].

error float

Numeric error under the ranking function (RMSE or BED). By convention +inf unless status is "ok"; this is not validated.

parameters ndarray | None

Fitted values, one per parameter in the order of parameter_labels, shape (n_parameters,), fixed values included; free_constants holds the specs they were fitted under. Set by the RMSE ranking only. None for other rankings and when nothing was fitted.

ranking_data dict[str, Any]

Freeform payload carried over from the RankingResult extra dict of the ranking function that scored this expression. Empty for rankings that emit nothing beyond score/parameters.

augmentations dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

Per-augmenter data keyed by augmenter name. Populated by ResultAugmenter subclasses via add_augmentation.

status Status

How the evaluation ended; see Status.

status_detail str | None

Why the status is not "ok": the parse error, the failed check of a required constraint (e.g. "MaxConstants: 9 constants, limit 8"), the exception, or the non-finite score. None for "ok".

advisory_violations list[CheckResult]

The failed checks of the evaluator's advisory constraints, as CheckResults with constraint and stage filled in; a check that raised is included, with error set. Pre-checks are recorded for every expression the evaluator could parse, whatever its status; post-checks only for models with status "ok". Pre-check results come first; within a stage, results follow the order of the constraints. Empty if no check failed, if the evaluator has no advisory constraints, or if the status is "invalid". It never affects error. See expression_constraints.

free_constants tuple[Constant, ...] | None

The specs parameters were fitted under (priors, bounds, fixed values), as Constants sorted by label; None when no specs were given. Parameters without a spec (bare C always), and a spec's unset prior or bounds, used EvalResult.default_constant.

Examples:

>>> result = ModelResult(expr=["C", "*", "X_0"], error=0.42)
>>> result.error, result.status
(0.42, 'ok')

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "ModelResult":
    """Reconstruct a [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult] from the output of [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict].

    Args:
        data: Dictionary produced by [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict],
            possibly after a JSON round trip. Unknown keys are ignored; a missing
            ``advisory_violations`` (results saved before it was recorded) loads as an empty
            list, a missing ``free_constants`` as ``None``; other malformed input has undefined
            behaviour. Each saved
            [CheckResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.CheckResult] comes back equal, field by field
            (an ``inf`` amount included).

    Returns:
        The reconstructed [ModelResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult].

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``data`` has no ``status`` (it was saved before statuses were recorded),
            or its ``status`` is not one of [STATUSES][SRToolkit.utils.types.STATUSES].
        ImportError: If the prior of a saved spec cannot be imported.

    Examples:
        >>> result = ModelResult(expr=["X_0", "+", "C"], error=0.25)
        >>> ModelResult.from_dict(result.to_dict()).expr
        ['X_0', '+', 'C']
    """
    if "status" not in data:
        raise ValueError(
            "[ModelResult.from_dict] This model was saved by an older SRToolkit version, without an "
            "evaluation status, and cannot be loaded. Rerun the experiment."
        )
    if data["status"] not in STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(f"[ModelResult.from_dict] Unknown status {data['status']!r}; expected one of {STATUSES}.")
    # Imported here: free_constants imports symbol_library, which imports this module.
    from .free_constants import Constant

    specs = data.get("free_constants")
    return cls(
        expr=data["expr"],
        error=data["error"],
        parameters=_from_json_safe(data["parameters"]),
        ranking_data=_from_json_safe(data["ranking_data"]),
        augmentations=_from_json_safe(data["augmentations"]),
        status=data["status"],
        status_detail=data["status_detail"],
        advisory_violations=[CheckResult(**r) for r in data.get("advisory_violations", [])],
        free_constants=None if specs is None else tuple(Constant.from_dict(c) for c in _from_json_safe(specs)),
    )

EvalResult(all_models: list[ModelResult], trace: list[int], approach_name: str, success_threshold: float | None = None, top_k: int = 20, dataset_name: str | None = None, metadata: dict | None = None, wall_time: float | None = None, augmentations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = dict(), default_constant: Constant | None = None, stop_reason: str | None = None, summary: RunSummary | None = None, checkpoint: dict[str, Any] | None = None, limits: list[dict[str, Any]] = list(), skips: dict[str, int] = dict())

Result of a single SR experiment, as returned by Results[i].

The stored data is the list of evaluated models and the evaluation trace; summary values such as min_error, best_expr, success and top_models() are derived from them. The ranking behind these summaries is cached. After construction models must not be modified or replaced, or the summaries can be stale.

A result of a long run can instead keep only its top models and a RunSummary (keep_all_models=False, see Evaluator.get_results); its methods then give the same answers, except where noted. All models of such a run stay in its checkpoint, if it was kept (see open_checkpoint).

Attributes:

Name Type Description all_models list[ModelResult]

All evaluated models, in the order they were first evaluated. trace indexes into this list. With a summary, only the top_k best models, best first.

trace list[int]

The evaluation trace. trace[k] is the index into all_models of the expression requested by the (k+1)-th counted call to evaluate_expr (a call that counts toward max_evaluations; see evaluator). Cache hits appear as repeated indices; calls made after evaluation was stopped are not recorded. Every entry must be a valid, non-negative index into all_models; otherwise behaviour is undefined. Empty with a summary.

approach_name str

Name of the SR approach, or empty string if not provided.

success_threshold float | None

The experiment succeeds if an error strictly below this is found. A nan threshold is never reached. None if not set.

top_k int

Default number of models returned by top_models(). 0 means none; negative means all models.

dataset_name str | None

Name of the dataset. None if not provided.

metadata dict | None

The evaluator's metadata without dataset_name (e.g. model name, seed, and the dataset's metadata under "dataset_metadata"). None if there is none.

wall_time float | None

Seconds the run took, all sessions of a resumed run together (see Evaluator.wall_time). None if not known, e.g. from a checkpoint of a run that crashed before its first commit.

augmentations dict[str, dict[str, Any]]

Per-augmenter data keyed by augmenter name. Populated by ResultAugmenter subclasses via add_augmentation.

default_constant Constant | None

The default spec of the run (a Constant template): the spec of every parameter without one of its own (see ModelResult.free_constants). With it, Expression(model.expr, symbol_library, model.free_constants).resolve(result.default_constant) (see Expression.resolve) gives the complete specs of a saved model. None for results saved in format 2.

stop_reason str | None

Why the run ended: "success_threshold", "max_evaluations", the reason of a callback (e.g. "time_limit") or of the approach (see stop), or "returned" if the search returned without stopping the evaluator. Any other reason than the first two marks a run that ended with budget left. None for results saved before it was recorded.

summary RunSummary | None

What is kept of the run instead of all its models, or None (default) if all_models and trace are complete.

checkpoint dict[str, Any] | None

A reference to the run's checkpoint, {"path": ..., "fingerprint": ...} (the absolute path and the evaluator's fingerprint, see Checkpoints), or None. Results.from_checkpoint, evaluate_approach and ExperimentJob.run set it when the file still exists as they return; get_results does not. Only open_checkpoint uses it.

limits list[dict[str, Any]]

The run's limit segments: one for its start and one per extension that changed something (a plain resume adds none; see Extending runs). Each is a dict with calls (the calls kept when the segment starts), max_evaluations (negative: no limit), success_threshold (None: none), callbacks (the to_dict() of each callback; [] if calls were made without callbacks, None if the segment made no call of evaluate_expr or count_skip) and previous_stop_reason (why the segment before ended; None for the first, or after a crash). Check extended beside stop_reason before comparing runs. [] if not recorded (results saved before it was, or built by hand).

skips dict[str, int]

How many expressions the approach skipped without evaluating them, by reason (see count_skip), e.g. {"evaluated": 12, "rejected": 3}. Evaluated calls are not counted: calls that repeat an evaluated model (cache hits) number evaluation_calls - num_evaluated, rejected calls status_counts(per="call")["rejected"]. {} if the approach reported none, or if not recorded (results saved before it was, or built by hand).

Examples:

>>> models = [ModelResult(expr=["X_0"], error=0.5), ModelResult(expr=["C", "*", "X_0"], error=0.05)]
>>> result = EvalResult(
...     all_models=models,
...     trace=[0, 1, 0],
...     approach_name="MyApproach",
...     success_threshold=0.1,
... )
>>> result.best_expr, result.min_error, result.success
('C*X_0', 0.05, True)

def top_models(self, k: int | None = None) -> list[ModelResult]:
    """Return the ``k`` best models, best first.

    Models with a finite error come first, sorted by error. Models whose error is not finite
    (``inf`` or ``nan``, not distinguished) come last. Only the error decides this, not the
    status; for results produced by the evaluator the two agree. Ties in error, and models
    that are all non-finite, are ordered by length (fewer tokens first), then by the order in
    which they were first evaluated. The returned objects are the ones in ``all_models``, not
    copies.

    Args:
        k: Number of models to return. Defaults to ``top_k``. ``0`` returns ``[]``; a negative
            value or one larger than the number of models returns all of them (with a
            ``summary``, the ``top_k`` kept ones).

    Returns:
        The best ``k`` models, best first.

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(expr=["X_0"], error=0.5), ModelResult(expr=["X_1"], error=0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1], approach_name="", top_k=1)
        >>> [m.expr for m in result.top_models()]
        [['X_1']]
        >>> [m.expr for m in result.top_models(k=-1)]
        [['X_1'], ['X_0']]
    """
    if k is None:
        k = self.top_k
    ranking = self._ranking()
    if 0 <= k < len(ranking):
        ranking = ranking[:k]
    return [self.all_models[i] for i in ranking]

def best_so_far(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Return the incumbent history: each call in the trace where the best error strictly improved.

    Failed models (non-finite error) never become the incumbent. Only a strictly lower error
    changes the incumbent, so after a tie broken by length the last entry need not be
    ``top_models(1)[0]``. With a ``summary``, read from ``summary.incumbents``, which also
    holds each model.

        A list of ``(call_number, model_index)`` pairs, where ``call_number`` is 1-based and
        ``model_index`` indexes into ``all_models`` (with a ``summary``, into the full run's

def calls_to_threshold(self, threshold: float | None = None) -> int | None:
    """Return the number of calls needed to first reach an error below ``threshold``.

    With a ``summary``, read from ``summary.incumbents`` (the same answer).

    Args:
        threshold: Error threshold. Defaults to ``success_threshold``.

    Returns:
        The 1-based call number at which an expression with a finite error strictly below
        ``threshold`` was first requested, or ``None`` if that never happened (always for a
        ``nan`` threshold). Failed models (non-finite error) never count. When aggregating
        over runs, treat
        ``None`` as censored at ``evaluation_calls`` rather than dropping the run (see
        [evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator]).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``threshold`` is not given and ``success_threshold`` is ``None``.

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["C"], 0.01)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 0, 1], approach_name="", success_threshold=0.1)
        >>> result.calls_to_threshold()
        3
    """
    if threshold is None:
        threshold = self.success_threshold
    if threshold is None:
        raise ValueError("[EvalResult.calls_to_threshold] No threshold given and success_threshold is None.")
    # Errors strictly decrease along the incumbents, so the first one below the threshold is the first call.
    return next((call for call, _, error in self._incumbents() if error < threshold), None)

def best_error_within(self, budgets: Sequence[int]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the best error found within each of the given numbers of counted calls.

    With a ``summary``, read from ``summary.incumbents`` (the same answer).

    A budget larger than ``evaluation_calls`` gets the run's final best error. This is exact
    for a run that reached ``success_threshold``, but only an upper bound for a run that
    stopped early for another reason (see [evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.evaluator]).
    Keep budgets at or below the experiment's ``max_evaluations``.

    Args:
        budgets: Numbers of calls, as ``int`` or numpy integers. Non-integers have undefined
            behaviour.

    Returns:
        Array of shape ``(len(budgets),)``, in the order of ``budgets``, with the best finite
        error within each budget.
        ``NaN`` where no model had been scored successfully yet, including every budget
        ``<= 0``.

    Examples:
        >>> failed = ModelResult(["X_0", "X_1"], float("inf"), status="invalid")
        >>> models = [failed, ModelResult(["X_1"], 0.5), ModelResult(["C"], 0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 2], approach_name="")
        >>> result.best_error_within([1, 2, 3, 10])
        array([nan, 0.5, 0.1, 0.1])
    """
    incumbents = self._incumbents()
    calls = [call for call, _, _ in incumbents]
    curve = np.full(len(budgets), np.nan)
    for j, budget in enumerate(budgets):
        position = bisect.bisect_right(calls, budget)  # incumbents found within the budget
        if position > 0:
            curve[j] = incumbents[position - 1][2]
    return curve

def status_counts(self, per: Literal["unique", "call"] = "unique") -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return the number of models with each [Status][SRToolkit.utils.types.Status].

    With a ``summary``, its stored counts.

    Args:
        per: ``"unique"`` counts each model (an expression with its specs) once; ``"call"`` counts every
            counted call in the trace, cache hits included.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with one entry per status in the order of
        [STATUSES][SRToolkit.utils.types.STATUSES], zeros included.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``per`` is not ``"unique"`` or ``"call"``.

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["X_0", "X_1"], float("inf"), status="invalid")]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 1], approach_name="")
        >>> result.status_counts()
        {'ok': 1, 'invalid': 1, 'rejected': 0, 'undefined': 0, 'error': 0}
        >>> result.status_counts(per="call")["invalid"]
        2
    """
    if per not in ("unique", "call"):
        raise ValueError(f"[EvalResult.status_counts] per must be 'unique' or 'call', got {per!r}.")
    if self.summary is not None:
        return dict(self.summary.status_counts if per == "unique" else self.summary.call_status_counts)
    models = self.all_models if per == "unique" else [self.all_models[i] for i in self.trace]
    counts = {status: 0 for status in STATUSES}
    for model in models:
        counts[model.status] += 1
    return counts

Return the models on the error-complexity Pareto front, shortest first.

The returned objects are the stored ones, not copies.

Raises:

Examples:

>>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["X_1"], 0.7), ModelResult(["C", "*", "X_0"], 0.1)]
>>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 2], approach_name="")
>>> ["".join(m.expr) for m in result.pareto_front()]
['X_0', 'C*X_0']

def pareto_front(self) -> list[ModelResult]:
    """Return the models on the error-complexity Pareto front, shortest first.

    Complexity is the number of tokens (``len(model.expr)``). Failed models (non-finite error)
    are excluded. Of the models of each length, the one with the lowest error is taken (the
    first evaluated on ties); it is on the front if its error is strictly lower than that of
    every shorter model on it. So errors strictly decrease along the front, and its last model
    is ``top_models(1)[0]`` whenever that has a finite error. With a ``summary``, read from
    ``summary.pareto_front``. The returned objects are the stored ones, not copies.

    Returns:
        The models on the front, by increasing length. Empty if no model has a finite error.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the result has a ``summary`` without a front (written before fronts were
            recorded).

    Examples:
        >>> models = [ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.5), ModelResult(["X_1"], 0.7), ModelResult(["C", "*", "X_0"], 0.1)]
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=models, trace=[0, 1, 2], approach_name="")
        >>> ["".join(m.expr) for m in result.pareto_front()]
        ['X_0', 'C*X_0']
    """
    if self.summary is not None:
        if self.summary.pareto_front is None:
            raise ValueError("[EvalResult.pareto_front] The summary of this result has no Pareto front.")
        return list(self.summary.pareto_front)
    best: dict[int, ModelResult] = {}  # per length, the first model with the lowest finite error
    for model in self.all_models:
        length = len(model.expr)
        if math.isfinite(model.error) and (length not in best or model.error < best[length].error):
            best[length] = model
    front: list[ModelResult] = []
    for length in sorted(best):
        if not front or best[length].error < front[-1].error:
            front.append(best[length])
    return front

def open_checkpoint(self, path: "str | os.PathLike | None" = None) -> "ModelStore":
    """Open the run's checkpoint read-only, to reach all its models.

    Its ``models`` and ``trace`` are read-only sequences that read from the file on demand, so
    a run of any length can be gone through without loading it (see
    [ModelStore][SRToolkit.evaluation.model_store.ModelStore]). Close it when done.

    Args:
        path: Where the checkpoint is now, if it was moved. Defaults to the path in
            ``checkpoint``. The fingerprint is checked either way.

    Returns:
        The checkpoint, opened with ``mode="read"``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``checkpoint`` is ``None``; if the file is a checkpoint of another run
            (its fingerprint differs from the one in ``checkpoint``; the message names the
            differing parts), which includes the run after an
            [extension][SRToolkit.dataset.dataset.Dataset.extend_run] that changed its
            limits; if it is not a checkpoint, or one of another format version.
        FileNotFoundError: If no file exists at the path; the message gives the path.
    """
    # Imported here: model_store imports this module.
    from SRToolkit.evaluation.model_store import ModelStore

    if self.checkpoint is None:
        raise ValueError("[EvalResult.open_checkpoint] This result has no checkpoint reference.")
    target = self.checkpoint["path"] if path is None else path
    store = ModelStore(target, "read")
    try:
        saved = store.get_header("fingerprint", {})
    except BaseException:
        store.close()
        raise
    expected = self.checkpoint["fingerprint"]
    changed = sorted(k for k in saved.keys() | expected.keys() if saved.get(k) != expected.get(k))
    if changed:
        store.close()
        hint = (
            " If the run was extended, use the extended run's results."
            if set(changed) <= {"max_evaluations", "success_threshold"}
            else ""
        )
        raise ValueError(
            f"[EvalResult.open_checkpoint] The checkpoint at {os.fspath(target)!r} is of another run: "
            f"these parameters differ: {', '.join(changed)}.{hint}"
        )
    return store

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Return a JSON-safe dictionary of this evaluation result.

    The dictionary can be passed to ``json.dump``. After a JSON round trip,
    [from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.from_dict] restores every field exactly
    (including ``metadata``, ``augmentations`` and each model, see
    [ModelResult.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict]), as guaranteed by
    [serialization][SRToolkit.utils.serialization]. The one exception is that numpy scalars come
    back as Python scalars.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with ``"format_version": 4`` and one entry per field
        (``default_constant`` as its ``to_dict``, ``summary`` as a dictionary of its fields
        with each model as its ``to_dict``, each ``None`` if not set). It also holds the
        derived summaries ``min_error``, ``best_expr``, ``success``, ``num_evaluated``,
        ``evaluation_calls`` and ``status_counts`` (per model), for reading the file
        directly (with a ``summary``, the counts are its own). ``from_dict`` ignores them.
        ``min_error`` is ``nan`` for a result without
        models, which ``json`` writes as the non-standard token ``NaN``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``metadata``, ``augmentations``, ``limits`` or ``skips`` contain a value that cannot be saved,
            or a model's ``to_dict`` raises (see
            [ModelResult.to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.to_dict]). The
            message gives its full path, e.g. ``all_models[3].ranking_data['z']``.

    Examples:
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=[ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.05)], trace=[0, 0], approach_name="MyApproach")
        >>> d = result.to_dict()
        >>> d["trace"], d["min_error"]
        ([0, 0], 0.05)
    """
    summary = None
    if self.summary is not None:
        summary = {
            "num_evaluated": self.summary.num_evaluated,
            "evaluation_calls": self.summary.evaluation_calls,
            "incumbents": [
                [call, index, model._to_dict(f"summary.incumbents[{i}].")]
                for i, (call, index, model) in enumerate(self.summary.incumbents)
            ],
            "status_counts": dict(self.summary.status_counts),
            "call_status_counts": dict(self.summary.call_status_counts),
            "pareto_front": (
                None
                if self.summary.pareto_front is None
                else [m._to_dict(f"summary.pareto_front[{i}].") for i, m in enumerate(self.summary.pareto_front)]
            ),
        }
    return {
        "format_version": 4,
        "min_error": float(self.min_error),
        "best_expr": self.best_expr,
        "success": self.success,
        "num_evaluated": self.num_evaluated,
        "evaluation_calls": self.evaluation_calls,
        "status_counts": self.status_counts(),
        "approach_name": self.approach_name,
        "dataset_name": self.dataset_name,
        "success_threshold": None if self.success_threshold is None else float(self.success_threshold),
        "top_k": int(self.top_k),
        "metadata": _to_json_safe(self.metadata, "metadata"),
        "wall_time": None if self.wall_time is None else float(self.wall_time),
        "stop_reason": self.stop_reason,
        "augmentations": _to_json_safe(self.augmentations, "augmentations"),
        "trace": [int(i) for i in self.trace],
        "all_models": [m._to_dict(f"all_models[{i}].") for i, m in enumerate(self.all_models)],
        "default_constant": (
            None
            if self.default_constant is None
            else _to_json_safe(self.default_constant.to_dict(), "default_constant")
        ),
        "summary": summary,
        "checkpoint": _to_json_safe(self.checkpoint, "checkpoint"),
        "limits": _to_json_safe(self.limits, "limits"),
        "skips": _to_json_safe(self.skips, "skips"),
    }

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "EvalResult":
    """Reconstruct an [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] from the output of [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.to_dict].

    Args:
        data: Dictionary produced by [to_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult.to_dict],
            possibly after a JSON round trip, of format 4, 3 (written before summaries and
            checkpoint references; ``summary`` and ``checkpoint`` load as ``None``) or 2
            (written before specs were recorded; ``default_constant`` and each model's
            ``free_constants`` load as ``None`` too). A missing ``stop_reason``, or a missing
            field of a saved ``summary`` that has a default, loads as ``None``; missing
            ``limits`` and ``skips`` load as ``[]`` and ``{}``. Unknown keys are
            ignored; other malformed input has undefined behaviour.

    Returns:
        The reconstructed [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult].

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is missing (results saved before the evaluation trace
            was recorded) or not ``2``, ``3`` or ``4``, or if a model cannot be loaded (see
            [ModelResult.from_dict][SRToolkit.utils.types.ModelResult.from_dict]).
        ImportError: If the prior of a saved spec cannot be imported.

    Examples:
        >>> result = EvalResult(all_models=[ModelResult(["X_0"], 0.05)], trace=[0], approach_name="MyApproach")
        >>> EvalResult.from_dict(result.to_dict()).best_expr
        'X_0'
    """
    fmt = data.get("format_version")
    if fmt not in (2, 3, 4):
        if fmt is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "[EvalResult.from_dict] These results were saved by an older SRToolkit version, without "
                "an evaluation trace, and cannot be loaded. Rerun the experiment; with ExperimentGrid, "
                "delete the old result files first, since existing files count as completed jobs."
            )
        raise ValueError(f"[EvalResult.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {fmt!r}. Expected 2, 3 or 4.")
    # Imported here: free_constants imports symbol_library, which imports this module.
    from .free_constants import Constant

    default = data.get("default_constant")
    summary = data.get("summary")
    if summary is not None:
        # A field with a default may be missing (saved before it existed): it loads as None.
        values = {
            f.name: summary.get(f.name) if f.default is not dataclasses.MISSING else summary[f.name]
            for f in dataclasses.fields(RunSummary)
        }
        values["incumbents"] = [(call, index, ModelResult.from_dict(m)) for call, index, m in values["incumbents"]]
        if values["pareto_front"] is not None:
            values["pareto_front"] = [ModelResult.from_dict(m) for m in values["pareto_front"]]
        summary = RunSummary(**values)
    return cls(
        all_models=[ModelResult.from_dict(m) for m in data["all_models"]],
        trace=list(data["trace"]),
        approach_name=data["approach_name"],
        success_threshold=data["success_threshold"],
        top_k=data["top_k"],
        dataset_name=data["dataset_name"],
        metadata=_from_json_safe(data["metadata"]),
        wall_time=data["wall_time"],
        augmentations=_from_json_safe(data["augmentations"]),
        default_constant=None if default is None else Constant.from_dict(_from_json_safe(default)),
        stop_reason=data.get("stop_reason"),
        summary=summary,
        checkpoint=_from_json_safe(data.get("checkpoint")),
        limits=_from_json_safe(data.get("limits", [])),
        skips=_from_json_safe(data.get("skips", {})),
    )

docs.title: SRToolkit.utils.units
docs.text:
Physical units of variables, constants and targets.

A Unit is a product of base dimensions raised to rational exponents, e.g. metres per second is m s^-1. The predefined units are constants of this module, named by their SI symbols, and combine with *, / and **:

from SRToolkit.utils import units as u

velocity = u.m / u.s
entropy = u.J / u.K
u.J == u.kg * u.m**2 / u.s**2  # True: derived units are products of base units

A misspelled name (u.meter) is an AttributeError. The predefined units are the seven SI base units m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd and the derived units N, J, W, Pa, Hz, C (coulomb), V, Ohm, F, T. A unit is a dimension, not a scale, so there are no prefixes: a kilometre has the unit m. State the scale of the data in the variable's VariableInfo description instead, e.g. VariableInfo("d", "distance in km", u.m). Checks such as ConsistentUnits treat km and m alike; a free constant absorbs the conversion factor.

docs.title: Custom units
docs.text:
Unit builds a unit from a dict of exponents. Its names must be predefined units, so a typo such as "meter" is an error, unless they are confirmed as custom units, e.g. for information or money:

from SRToolkit.utils.units import Unit

rate = Unit({"bit": 1, "s": -1}, custom_units=["bit"])
BIT = Unit({"bit": 1}, custom_units=["bit"])  # or name it once and combine
rate == BIT / u.s  # True

custom_units declares new base dimensions. A unit made of existing ones is built with arithmetic instead, e.g. a litre is u.m**3: Unit({"L": 1}, custom_units=["L"]) would be a new dimension that does not match m^3.

docs.title: Saving and reading
docs.text: to_dict writes a unit as {dimension: exponent} over base dimensions, with the exponents as strings ({"m": "1", "s": "-1"}), and from_dict rebuilds it without confirmation: a saved unit was valid when it was made. str is for reading only: "kg m^2 s^-2", "m^(1/2)", and "1" for the dimensionless unit Unit(). str, to_dict and dimensions list base dimensions by name in Python string order, so uppercase comes first: A K cd kg m mol s.

docs.title: How symbols act on units
docs.text:
A UnitRule says how an operator or function combines the units of its arguments, e.g. * multiplies them and sin needs a dimensionless argument. Every "op" and "fn" symbol of a SymbolLibrary has one (see add_symbol), so a custom symbol is described once, where it is defined:

from fractions import Fraction

from SRToolkit.utils import FN_PREFIX, SymbolLibrary
from SRToolkit.utils.units import UnitRule

sl = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(2)
sl.add_symbol("cbrt", "fn", FN_PREFIX, "np.cbrt({})", unit_rule=UnitRule.power(Fraction(1, 3)))

Units are used by ConsistentUnits, by VariableInfo and by the grammar constraint DimensionalConsistency.

Unit(units: Mapping[str, int | Fraction] | None = None, custom_units: Iterable[str] = ())

A physical unit: base dimensions with rational exponents.

Immutable (assigning an attribute raises AttributeError) and hashable; units can be copied and pickled. Two units are equal when they have the same base dimensions with the same exponents, however they were built.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default units Mapping[str, int | Fraction] | None

Exponents by unit name, e.g. {"m": 1, "s": -1}. A name is a predefined unit (see the module docstring; a derived unit such as "J" stands for its base dimensions) or a name in custom_units. Exponents are int or Fraction; zero exponents are dropped. None (the default) gives the dimensionless unit.

None custom_units Iterable[str]

Names of custom base dimensions that units may use, e.g. ["bit"]; a single string is one name. Each must be a valid Python identifier. A predefined name always means the predefined unit.

()

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a name in units is neither predefined nor in custom_units (the message names it and lists the predefined units), or a name in custom_units is not a valid Python identifier.

TypeError

If an exponent is not an int or a Fraction.

Examples:

>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from SRToolkit.utils import units as u
>>> v = Unit({"m": 1, "s": -1})
>>> v == u.m / u.s
True
>>> str(Unit({"J": 1, "K": -1}))
'K^-1 kg m^2 s^-2'
>>> str(Unit({"bit": 1, "s": -1}, custom_units=["bit"]))

>>> str(u.m ** Fraction(1, 2))

Source code in SRToolkit/utils/units.py 
def __init__(self, units: Mapping[str, int | Fraction] | None = None, custom_units: Iterable[str] = ()) -> None:
    custom = {custom_units} if isinstance(custom_units, str) else set(custom_units)
    invalid = sorted((n for n in custom if not (isinstance(n, str) and n.isidentifier())), key=repr)
    if invalid:
        raise ValueError(f"Unit: custom unit names must be valid Python identifiers, got {invalid}.")
    dims: dict[str, Fraction] = {}
    for name, exponent in (units or {}).items():
        if not isinstance(exponent, (int, Fraction)) or isinstance(exponent, bool):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Unit: the exponent of {name!r} must be an int or a Fraction, got {type(exponent).__name__}."
            )
        if name in _DERIVED_UNITS:
            base: Mapping[str, int | Fraction] = _DERIVED_UNITS[name]
        elif name in _BASE_UNITS or name in custom:
            base = {name: 1}
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unit: {name!r} is not a predefined unit ({', '.join((*_BASE_UNITS, *_DERIVED_UNITS))}); "
                f"confirm a custom unit with custom_units=[{name!r}]."
            )
        for dim, k in base.items():
            dims[dim] = dims.get(dim, Fraction(0)) + Fraction(exponent) * k
    object.__setattr__(self, "_dims", tuple(sorted((name, exp) for name, exp in dims.items() if exp != 0)))

def __mul__(self, other: Unit) -> Unit:
    """Return the product of two units: exponents of the same dimension add.

    Args:
        other: A unit.

    Returns:
        The product.
    """
    if not isinstance(other, Unit):
        return NotImplemented
    dims = dict(self._dims)
    for name, exp in other._dims:
        dims[name] = dims.get(name, Fraction(0)) + exp
    return Unit(dims, custom_units=dims)

def __truediv__(self, other: Unit) -> Unit:
    """Return the quotient of two units: the exponents of ``other`` are subtracted.

    Args:

    if not isinstance(other, Unit):

    return self * other**-1

def __pow__(self, exponent: int | Fraction) -> Unit:
    """Return the unit raised to a rational power: every exponent is multiplied by it.

    Args:
        exponent: An ``int`` or a ``Fraction``. ``0`` gives the dimensionless unit.

    Returns:
        The power.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``exponent`` is not an ``int`` or a ``Fraction`` (e.g. a ``float``).
    """
    if not isinstance(exponent, (int, Fraction)) or isinstance(exponent, bool):
        raise TypeError(f"Unit: the power must be an int or a Fraction, got {type(exponent).__name__}.")
    dims = {name: exp * exponent for name, exp in self._dims}
    return Unit(dims, custom_units=dims)

def __str__(self) -> str:
    """Return the unit as text: ``"1"`` if dimensionless, otherwise the factors in name order.

    A factor is ``<name>`` for exponent 1, ``<name>^<k>`` for another integer (``s^-2``) and
    ``<name>^(<p>/<q>)`` for a fraction, the sign inside the brackets (``m^(-1/2)``), separated
    by single spaces.

    Returns:
        The text, e.g. ``"kg m^2 s^-2"``.
    """
    if not self._dims:
        return "1"
    factors = []
    for name, exp in self._dims:
        if exp == 1:
            factors.append(name)
        else:
            factors.append(f"{name}^{exp.numerator if exp.denominator == 1 else f'({exp})'}")
    return " ".join(factors)

How an operator or function combines the units of its arguments.

Immutable (assigning an attribute raises AttributeError) and hashable; rules can be copied and pickled, and are compared by kind and exponent. Use the class attributes and power; the constructor is not part of the API.

Rule Arity Result Conflict when SAME 1 or 2 the arguments' unit with two arguments, their units differ MULTIPLY 2 product of the units never DIVIDE 2 left unit divided by right unit never EXPONENT 2 if the exponent is a single number token (defined in ConsistentUnits), the base unit to that power; otherwise dimensionless the exponent is not a number token and the base or the exponent is not dimensionless power(k) 1 the argument's unit to the power k never DIMENSIONLESS 1 or 2 dimensionless an argument is not dimensionless
